info.title: Nexus API
info.description:
The one Nexus API: Nexus Gateway's own endpoints plus every registered capability at /v1/{product}/{capability}/{verb}. This file holds Gateway's part; GET /v1/openapi.json serves it merged with each module's and connector's operations. MVP: not a stable contract yet.

## Permissions

Every operation names the action it needs in `x-nexus-permission`; the router checks it before the handler runs. A lead is a member who leads at least one team. A service account's key (`nxsa_…`) holds the public endpoints only, until a Policy Engine statement admits it to more. An agent link's token (`nxo_…`) is no column: it holds what the person who linked it granted, cut down to that person's role now.

| Action | Owner | Admin | Lead | Member | Service account | Sandbox | Module key | Signed out | Covers |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | --- |

| `desktop.revoke` | ✓ | ✓ | – | – | – | – | – | – | Read and change the desktop app versions this Gateway refuses with 426 desktop_revoked, for every organization (a person with a platform role only) |
| `staff.read` | ✓ | ✓ | – | – | – | – | – | – | Read every person's and organization's metadata and usage across organizations, audited (a person with a platform role who is one of Nexus's own people only) |

## Operators

A Nexus operator, a person with a platform role, reaches a customer's organization only under an operator grant (`POST /v1/operator-grants`: a reason, a list of actions and an expiry). The operator sends its own person token and the header `x-nexus-operator-grant: opg_…`. The request then runs in the customer's organization, and may do only the actions the grant names that an admin may do: the operator's own role in their organization adds nothing. No grant reaches the model and chat calls, the coding-agent gateway, the operator's own keys and tokens, or the organization switch. Before the request runs, Gateway writes `operator.request` in the customer's audit log (the operator's user id, the grant id, the method, the path and the action; never an email). If that write fails, the request is a 503 `operator_log_unavailable` and does not run. An unknown, expired or revoked grant, a grant held by another person, and a person whose platform role was revoked are all a 403 `operator_grant_invalid`. The header is a 400 with a module key, a service account key or Nexus UI's secret, and on a public endpoint. The customer's owners and admins read the grants (`GET /v1/operator-grants`) and revoke them (`DELETE /v1/operator-grants/{id}`).

## Idempotency

Writes and model calls accept an `Idempotency-Key` header (see the parameter); the `nexus` CLI sends one on every mutating command.

## Rate limits

Every request the gateway authenticates (every operation but the `public` and `ui.session` ones) counts against its caller's limit, a fixed one-minute window. Its answer carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` (whole seconds until the window starts over); past the limit it is a 429 `rate_limit_error` that adds `Retry-After`.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway
tags.description: Organizations, keys, models, spend and the module registry.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Chat
tags.description: Chat sessions, Nexus UI's home and `nexus chat`. Two modes: Chat, with any model you may use, and Ask your code, grounded in your organization's Nexus Wiki. Sessions are private to their author; messages are kept for the organization's retention window (90 days by default, GET/PUT /v1/orgs/settings).

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Artifacts
tags.description: Nexus Artifacts: a chat session shared as an immutable snapshot (its messages, sources, the model of each answer, mode, title, author and cost). Inside the organization: the whole organization, chosen teams or chosen people. Outside it, as the organization's settings allow (`artifacts.external*`: on, with public links, by default): named people by email, who open it signed in with that verified email (a forwarded link opens for nobody else, who can ask for access), or anyone with an unguessable link, never indexed, optionally expiring. Readers outside see the author's name and the organization's name, never the cost, the author's email or team names, and Ask your code's sources only when the organization allows it and the author included them. Sharing again makes a new version; each version survives the chat being edited or deleted, is revocable at once, and is kept for the organization's chat retention from the moment it was shared. Owners and admins see everything shared outside, with open counts, and revoke in bulk. Every artifact and chat downloads as Markdown.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Pages
tags.description: Pages: standalone HTML, Markdown, React (`jsx`) or spreadsheet (`sheet`, JSON data) pages, and whiteboards (`board`, JSON data that every version must parse as, else 400 `page_board_invalid` with `nexus.problems`; a board may be written as a layout, a timeline, columns, a flow, a mind map or a grid, which Gateway lays out on top of the latest version, else 400 `page_board_layout_invalid`), in versions that never change. Every write makes the next version; a write built on an old version is refused (409 `page_version_conflict`), and a restore makes a new version from an old one. At most 16 MiB a version. Writes that contain what phishing needs (password fields, forms that submit somewhere, meta refresh, iframes, object and embed, obfuscated eval) are refused with the reason (400 `page_content_blocked`). Private to their owner for now: sharing and the sandboxed viewer come next.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Design systems
tags.description: Nexus Design's design systems: the tokens and notes designs are made, served and checked with.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Skills
tags.description: Skills: a person's own SKILL.md files (the open format), in versions that never change. A skill belongs to the person, whichever organization they are signed in to; someone else's skill is a 404. Every write makes the next version; a write built on an old version is refused (409 `skill_version_conflict`). A file is at most 1 MiB. A person keeps at most 200 skills (409 `skill_limit`) and a skill at most 500 versions (400 `skill_version_limit`). The file starts with YAML front matter that has a `name` (1 to 64 characters of `a-z`, `0-9` and single hyphens) and a `description` (1 to 1024 characters). A file that does not is refused with a code that says why: `invalid_frontmatter`, `missing_name`, `invalid_name`, `missing_description`, `invalid_description` or `skill_too_large` (413). Export returns the file byte for byte. Load records (`/v1/skill-loads`) say which skill and version a session loaded in web chat or was delivered by a launcher; a record holds no skill text and stays when the skill is deleted. Promotions (`/v1/skill-promotions`): a person asks to share one version of their skill with the organization or a team, and an approver who is not that person approves or refuses it. The request is a copy; the skill stays the person's own.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Devices
tags.description: Devices: a person's device keys and device pairing for end-to-end encrypted session sync. Each device makes its own key pairs and sends only the public keys: an X25519 key that each thread's content key is locked to (HPKE), and an Ed25519 key it signs with. Gateway stores the public keys and the locked copies and cannot open any of them. A device belongs to the person, whichever organization they are signed in to; someone else's is a 404. The person's first device is trusted at once. Every later one is pending until a trusted device signs its id and keys, and a revocation needs a trusted device's signature too, so signing in alone never adds or removes a trusted device.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Models
tags.description: The model catalog (supported and coming soon), model access policies (allow and deny lists per organization, team and coding agent; a deny always wins; levels only narrow), and the policy test. Nexus calls providers directly.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Explorer
tags.description: The Explorer's data: every model's LMArena, Vals AI and Hugging Face numbers, the catalog's status and list prices, the boards, each model's rating history and the market series, polled once a day. Public, read-only and cacheable: each answer carries an ETag (a request with `If-None-Match` gets a 304) and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`. Only cleared sources' numbers are served. Without a server setting, 503 `not_configured`; before the first poll, 503 `no_data`.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Agents
tags.description: `nexus claude` and `nexus codex`: model policy and sessions. The agents' model calls go through the agent gateway, where each is reserved, metered, checked against the organization's policy and attributed to the person and their session.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Agent API
tags.description: Your own agent, the one `@nexus` is in Slack, through Gateway: `/v1/agent/*` forwards to the agent API with your token. Off unless the Gateway turns it on.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Agent gateway
tags.description: The Anthropic Messages API and the OpenAI Responses API, passed through to the provider. Authenticate with a personal Nexus token (`nexus auth login`) or API key (`Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`); any member may call. Requests and responses, streaming included, are the providers' own; errors use the provider's error shape. Every call is reserved before it is forwarded and settled on the reported usage; a call over budget is refused with 402.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Jobs
tags.description: Jobs: a module's verb with its input, run in the background for the member who submitted it. A job is `accepted`, then `running`, then `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Its id is derived from the submit's `Idempotency-Key`, so a resend names the same job. A job is its creator's and its organization's owners' and admins'; to anyone else it does not exist.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Cloud machines
tags.description: Cloud machines: a Linux machine at a cloud provider (boat.dev in v1) for each person, on Nexus's own provider account. Nobody opens a provider account or sees Nexus's key. Gateway charges a machine's running time to the organization as cloud compute (product `cloud`, capability `compute` in GET /v1/spend), at the provider's price per second, when it sleeps or is deleted and every 15 minutes while it runs. A machine is its person's alone: to anyone else it does not exist. One live machine per person in an organization. Without a provider account on the Gateway, every route answers 503 `cloud_unavailable`.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Cloud sessions
tags.description: Headless cloud sessions: a cloud session that starts with no desktop app, for the assistant, the CLI, MCP and the apps. Each session runs on its own cloud machine of yours, with the cloud machines' limits and charges. A session is its person's alone: to anyone else it does not exist. Off unless a server setting is on: every route then answers 404.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Cloud sandboxes
tags.description: Cloud sandboxes: a module's throwaway machine at a cloud provider (boat.dev in v1), on Nexus's own provider account, for commands Nexus does not trust. Nexus Review's agent runs its commands in one. Only Nexus Review's module key may use them (`cloud.sandboxes.use`, product `robustness`, capability `review`). A sandbox gets no Nexus token and no files. At most a server setting live at once; one more is refused, with no queue. Gateway charges a sandbox's running time to the organization as cloud compute (product `cloud`, capability `compute` in GET /v1/spend), from its create to its delete, and deletes it at its `expiresAt`. Without a provider account on the Gateway, every route answers 503 `cloud_unavailable`.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Fix runs
tags.description: Fix runs, for `@nexus fix this`: Gateway fixes one GitHub issue in a throwaway cloud sandbox on Nexus's provider account and opens the pull request as the person's agent. The run reads the issue and the repository through the GitHub connector, runs the coding agent's turns through Gateway, and runs every command in the sandbox with no network and no credential. It opens the pull request with `github/pull_create` through the person's agents' writes, so only an agent link starts one. A run is a job: its state and its pull request are read at `GET /v1/cloud/runs/{id}`. The sandbox is charged as cloud compute. Rust only.

tags.name: Connectors
tags.description: Connector reads and module writes with a standing Policy grant, shared by every module.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Auth
tags.description: `nexus auth login` (a device code approved in Nexus UI), personal tokens and API keys.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Orgs
tags.description: An organization's members and roles (one owner, admins, members), ownership and budget. When the sign-in provider holds the organization, its roles change through Nexus UI, which updates the provider first.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › GitHub
tags.description: The Nexus GitHub App, linked repositories and their Nexus Wiki runs.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Slack
tags.description: The Nexus Slack app: an owner or admin binds a Slack workspace to the organization through Slack's OAuth install, and confirms it. A workspace binds to one organization at a time. The bot token is sealed in the vault and never shown.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Teams
tags.description: Teams, the levels between the organization and the person, kept in Gateway (the sign-in provider has no teams). Teams nest: a team may have a parent team (no cycles, at most 10 levels) and a `level`, a free-text label each organization chooses. Someone added by an email not in the organization yet is a pending member until they join it. An organization can load its whole tree from a file (`POST /v1/teams/import`). Owners and admins create, rename and delete teams and manage their members; every member reads them and sets their own default team. Spend is attributed to the team named with `x-nexus-team` (or a `team` field), else the caller's default team. Team caps and person budgets are built: see Budgets. Team model policies are built: see Models.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Budgets
tags.description: Spend limits per person and calendar month (UTC), checked with the organization's balance when every call reserves (chat completions, the agent gateway, module runs, chat sessions). The organization sets a default limit per person and overrides per person, both stored at the organization; no default means no person limit. Owners and admins also cap a team per UTC day, week or month (`PUT /v1/teams/{slug}/budget`): the cap is a pool for the team and every team under it. A call that would go over a person limit, a team cap or the organization's budget is refused with 402 `budget_exceeded`, naming the level, and counted as an overspend prevented. The 402 says what is left for the caller; only a person's 402 also names its limit. Person limits reset on the 1st at 00:00 UTC.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Analytics
tags.description: Usage over a date range grouped by team, person, model, provider, product, key or day. Owners and admins see the organization; members see their own usage and their teams'. by team, `depth` and `under` roll spend up the tree of teams.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Audit
tags.description: The append-only audit log: who changed what, through which credential, from which surface, before and after.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Service accounts
tags.description: Service accounts: callers for CI and scripts. An owner or admin makes one, a member answers for it, a team owns it, and it expires (365 days at most). It is no member and holds no seat. Its keys (`nxsa_…`) are stored as a hash and shown once (a replay of the same `Idempotency-Key` within 24 hours shows one again), live 90 days by default, and stop when the account is revoked or expires, its owner leaves the organization, or its team is deleted. They reach the public endpoints only, until a Policy Engine statement admits them to more.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Operator grants
tags.description: Operator grants: the one way a Nexus operator reaches a customer's organization. A person with a platform role (`operator` or `platform_admin`) asks for a grant with a reason, a list of actions and an expiry (24 hours by default, 7 days at most). The customer's owners and admins read every grant, and every act under it in their audit log, and revoke it at once. A grant makes no member and no seat. The operator then sends its own person's API key or token with the header `x-nexus-operator-grant: opg_…`. The header can give: 400 `invalid_operator_grant` (not one `opg_…` id), 400 `operator_header_refused` (with a module key, a service account key, Nexus UI's server or a public endpoint), 403 `operator_grant_invalid` (unknown, ended, revoked, held by another person, or its operator's platform role was revoked), 403 `operator_scope` (the grant does not name the route's action) and 503 `operator_log_unavailable` (the `operator.request` audit event could not be written, so the request did not run).

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Staff
tags.description: Reads across organizations for Nexus's own people only: a person with a platform role who is marked staff or signs in with a Nexus address. Each read is audited in the caller's organization before it runs. Metadata and counts only, never content.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Agent links
tags.description: Agent links: the credential of an agent that acts for one person. A person links an agent and names what it may do (`models.use`, `spend.read_own`, `connectors.use`, `chat.ask`, `chat.web`, `agents.memory`). Its token (`nxo_…`) is stored as a hash and shown once. The agent holds that grant cut down to the person's role now, and never the routes that are the person's alone. The person, or an owner or admin, unlinks it, and the person's own tokens do not change.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Developer clients
tags.description: The OAuth clients a person registered for their forks of Nexus's apps.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Routines
tags.description: Routines: work your agent does for you without being asked, such as a morning brief. A routine has an owner, a trigger, an action, proactivity and caps. It runs as its owner only, reads and notifies only, and owns one Runtime schedule whose slots each start one job. It is its owner's, and its organization's owners' and admins' to read, pause and delete; to anyone else it does not exist.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Session store
tags.description: The session store: end-to-end encrypted session sync. A runner (the desktop app, `nexus-host`) seals each event of a thread with the thread's content key and uploads it in order; the person's other trusted devices read the events back and open them on the device. Gateway stores bytes it cannot open, plus the usage numbers budgets need: agent, model, tokens, cost, status and times. The title and the repository are inside the sealed events. A thread belongs to the person and the organization of its first upload; anyone else's is a 404. Its locked content keys are under Devices.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Projects
tags.description: Projects (behind a server setting; off, each route answers 404): an organization's record that groups repositories and people. Owners and admins are admins of every project. Only a project admin changes its repositories and members; anyone in it reads it.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Operator grants
tags.description: Operator grants: the one way a Nexus operator reaches a customer's organization. An owner or admin of a tenant-zero organization asks for a grant with a reason, a list of actions and an expiry (24 hours by default, 7 days at most). The customer's owners and admins read every grant, and every act under it in their audit log, and revoke it at once. A grant makes no member and no seat. The operator then sends its own person's API key or token with the header `x-nexus-operator-grant: opg_…`. The header can give: 400 `invalid_operator_grant` (not one `opg_…` id), 400 `operator_header_refused` (with a module key, a service account key, Nexus UI's server or a public endpoint), 403 `operator_grant_invalid` (unknown, ended, revoked, held by another person, or its operator left the admins of tenant zero), 403 `operator_scope` (the grant does not name the route's action) and 503 `operator_log_unavailable` (the `operator.request` audit event could not be written, so the request did not run).

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Staff
tags.description: Reads across organizations for Nexus's own people only: an owner or admin of a tenant-zero organization who is marked staff or signs in with a Nexus address. Each read is audited in tenant zero before it runs. Metadata and counts only, never content.

tags.name: Nexus Gateway › Apps
tags.description: Nexus Apps: an app you deploy from a folder, hosted on Vercel in Nexus's own team (Vercel for Platforms, one Vercel project per app). Nobody needs a Vercel account. Nexus pays Vercel for every app on its team, so an organization holds at most a server setting apps (10 by default); a claim link moves an app's project to your own Vercel account, where it stops costing Nexus. Each app shows what Vercel billed for it, from Vercel's daily charges. An app is its deployer's, and the organization's owners and admins reach every app; to anyone else it does not exist. Off unless the Gateway sets a server setting: then every route answers 404 `apps_off`, and these routes are left out of GET /v1/openapi.json. On, without the server settings, every route answers 503 `apps_unavailable`.

post.summary: OpenAI-compatible chat completion. Policy check, then the call's maximum cost is reserved against the budget, the provider is called, and the reservation settles on reported usage (also on errors). Model `nexus/auto` lets Gateway choose. `model` is a catalog id (any spelling), `nexus/auto` or `nexus/default` (the effective default within policy); the answer's `model` and `x-nexus-model` header say which model ran. An answer the auto router picked also names the router version in `x-nexus-router` and in `nexus.router`. A refused model: 403 `model_not_allowed` (policy, naming the level and rule), 404 `model_not_found`, 400 `model_not_supported` (coming soon); never sent upstream or reserved, recorded as a refused call. Who pays: the organization's own key; Nexus's own key for Nexus's own organizations; Nexus credit only for a module run's scoped key (a Nexus feature, such as a Wiki or Review run). Any other caller with no key of its own gets 403 `provider_key_required`, never Nexus credit. Tools (OpenAI's `tools`, `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls`, an assistant's `tool_calls` and `tool` messages) work for Anthropic and OpenAI models alike, translated by Gateway. `stream: true` answers as server-sent events in OpenAI's `chat.completion.chunk` shape (the role, then text and tool-call pieces, a chunk with `finish_reason`, a last chunk with no choices and the `usage` and `nexus` cost, then `data: [DONE]`; a failure after the stream started is a `data: {"error": …}` event), so agent tools that speak Chat Completions (opencode's `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` and the like) use `<gateway>/v1` as their provider. A stream is checked, reserved and refused exactly as a call that does not stream, and settles however it ends: on the reported usage, or on what streamed when the provider fails or the caller goes away.

200.description: OK: the answer, or with `stream: true` its server-sent events

402.description: The call's maximum cost is more than the budget left (`budget_exceeded`; `subsidy_exhausted` for the Nexus subsidy, or `credit_exhausted` for the organization's prepaid credits), or the organization has an unpaid Nexus invoice past its grace (`payment_past_due`). A `budget_exceeded` refusal carries `notified: true` in its details once Gateway has told the refused person and the organization's owners and admins. The details are a BudgetRefusal: each money figure with its exact decimal twin.

502.description: The provider failed the call. `upstream_auth`: it refused the provider key the call ran on (its 401), never your Nexus API key. `upstream_forbidden`: it refused this model for that key (its 403); the key may still serve other models. `upstream_billing`: the provider account behind that key is out of credit (its 402), never your Nexus budget. The message says whose key it was: your organization's own, Nexus's, or the Nexus credit's. Any other provider 5xx is a 502 with no code.

503.description: The provider's or the Gateway's own; every one may be retried. The provider's: it has no capacity now (its 529, or the 503 OpenAI documents as its overload), `upstream_overloaded`; retry after its `retry-after` when it sent one, or try another model. The Gateway's: it is at its limit of requests in flight (`overloaded`, retry after 1 s); it is stopping and takes no new request (`draining`, retry after 5 s); it stopped before the call's first event (`gateway_stopping`, send the call again: it reaches a running Gateway); or its database is busy (`database_busy`: nothing was committed, retry shortly).

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait: 1 on `overloaded`, 5 on `draining`, the provider's own on `upstream_overloaded` when it sent one; none on `gateway_stopping` or `database_busy`.

post.summary: Submit a job: the verb of a module to run, with its input. `module` is `<product>/<capability>` (`intelligence/wiki`), the path of the verb's own route, and the caller needs the action the module declares for the verb (`wiki.run` for Nexus Wiki's `run`), as on that route. Needs an `Idempotency-Key`: the job's id is derived from it, with the organization and the credential, so a resend names the job the first send made. For 24 hours a resend replays the first answer (202, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`), even after the job has moved on. After that it answers 200 with the job as it is now. A resend with a different `module`, `verb` or `input` is a 422 `idempotency_key_reused`. `team` (or `x-nexus-team`) names the team the job's model calls go to; the caller's default team when absent. A job stays `accepted` until a worker takes it.

post.summary: Create the cloud machine of a desktop session. Send `sessionId` and the session's `title`: a create for a session that has a live machine returns that machine. Nexus names and sizes every machine, so `name` and `size` are read and ignored. The machine starts from Nexus's image, with its own Nexus token in `~/.nexus/host/credentials`; deleting the machine revokes that token. Send an `Idempotency-Key`: the machine's id is derived from it, so a resend names the machine the first send made, and finishes it when the provider's answer was lost. A machine that cannot start now waits in the queue (202, state `queued`): Gateway runs its most machines, the person runs their share, the person started 20 machines and gets one more every 5 minutes, or the provider is at its limits. The meter starts the queue oldest first. A person asks for at most 200 starts (creates and wakes) in a UTC day, and an organization's people 500 together: one more answers 429 `cloud_daily_starts` until 00:00 UTC (`Retry-After`). An organization with only the free start is on the trial: it runs one machine at a time, and all trial organizations together a few. A trial machine never waits in the queue: one more answers 429 `cloud_trial_limit` or `cloud_trial_busy` (`Retry-After`), which name Billing. Credits, a card or a contract lift the trial. A person keeps at most 50 machines, asleep or not: one more answers 429 `cloud_machine_limit`. Read the queued machine (GET) while you wait: one nobody read for 10 minutes ends, `failed`. Its running time is charged as cloud compute from its start.

The refusal is recorded. When a running machine's next 15 minutes are refused, Gateway puts it to sleep, with `stopReason` `budget`.

It reads `ready`, with provider `own`; `hostOnline` says whether it answers. Nexus never starts, stops, sizes or charges it, and any organization may pair one. A second pairing with the same token answers the same machine. A person pairs at most 10 servers (409 `own_servers_full`).

post.summary: A cloud machine's heartbeat, sent by its host (`nexus-host`) every minute with the machine's own Nexus token (the one in `~/.nexus/host/credentials`): whether its agent works, since when it is idle, the person's last interaction and the kernel's out-of-memory kill count. Gateway stores the last report. A time after now is taken as now. The report never extends the machine's longest run (a server setting, from the person's last create, wake or access). Gateway puts the machine to sleep (`idle`) when its agent was idle 5 minutes and its person did not interact for 20 minutes, and never while its agent works. A machine whose host sends no report for 15 minutes (or never sent one) sleeps 20 minutes after its last interaction, create, wake or access. A rise in the out-of-memory count restarts the machine one size bigger, up to `large` (`resize`).

Gateway asks the host to open its side and joins the two. Each text and binary frame and the close pass on as they came. Gateway reads and stores no frame. A frame is at most 16 MiB. Gateway pings every 20 seconds. When the host does not open its side within 10 seconds, the stream closes with 1013 (try again later); when Gateway stops, with 1012. A joined stream counts as an interaction, as an access does. Gateway holds the streams in memory, on one copy.

post.summary: Take the session as its runner: the desktop app, nexus-host or a cloud machine that runs its agent. The runner gets the session's next fencing token and a lease of 60 seconds, which it renews every 20 seconds (POST /v1/sessions/{id}/runner/renew). Without `seenToken`, the take succeeds only when no runner's lease is live: the first take, or a takeover after the lease passed. With `seenToken` (the session's `fencingToken` as you read it), it is a handoff: it takes the session from whoever holds it, while that is still the session's token. Each take raises the token by one, so the runner it replaced gets 409 `lost_runner` on its next renewal or connector write. Of two takes at once, one wins and the other gets 409 `takeover_conflict`.

post.summary: Run one connector operation, a read or a change. A change runs only for a module holding a write grant for it (PUT /v1/policies/grants/{product}/{capability}); a person's change is refused with 403 `write_not_granted` until people get write scopes. A chat agent's link writes only with the approval record the person confirmed for exactly this call, named in `x-nexus-approval`, while the organization has chat writes on: else 403 `write_not_granted` (no record), `approval_invalid` or `chat_writes_off`. The record is used by the call, once. Every change attempt and every scoped read is audited as `connector.write`. `github/pull_merge` squash-merges only at `expected_head_sha` and only when branch protection allows it, never past it: 400 `merge_method_refused`, 409 `head_changed`, `not_mergeable` or `pull_not_open`. `github/pull_edit` and `pull_reviewers` change only an open pull request (409 `pull_not_open`), and GitHub's refusal of a reviewer is 422 `reviewer_refused`. `github/pull_state` closes or reopens and never merges: 409 `pull_merged`, 422 `not_reopenable`. `github/pull_labels` adds only a label the repository has: 404 `label_unknown`. A runner's change inside a native session names the session and its fencing token (`x-nexus-cloud-session`, `x-nexus-fencing-token`): 400 `invalid_session_fence` without both, 404 `session_not_found` for a session that is not yours, 409 `session_ended` for an ended one, and 409 `lost_runner` when another runner took the session; nothing is called, and the refusal is audited. A change that names no fence while its credential holds a native session's live runner lease is refused with 409 `fence_required` (`error.nexus.session` names the session) when the server requires the fence; nothing is called, and the refusal is audited. When the server asks for write scopes on demand, a change on an OAuth connection that holds none of the connector's write scopes is refused with 403 `write_consent_required`; nothing is called. `error.nexus` names the `connector`, the `account`, the `scopes` the change needs, and the `consent` call that asks for them (POST /v1/connections/{connector}/oauth with `access: write`). A change sent with `Idempotency-Key` carries a hidden marker in the body it writes (`github/issue_comment`, `pull_review`, `issue_create`). When GitHub got the write but its answer was lost, the 502 says `error.nexus.outcome: unknown` and the key is kept: a retry with the same key reads the target for the marker, answers what it found as a replay, or writes once. A retry that cannot read the target is 502 `reconciliation_failed` and writes nothing. Send an `Idempotency-Key` with every change. While the Gateway enforces connector write keys (off by default), a change without one is 428 `idempotency_key_required`, and nothing is called. A read never needs one.

get.summary: This document, merged with every registered module's operations.
Liveness: the process answers. It reads no database, and it stays 200 while Gateway drains.
get.description: Outside `/v1`: no credential, no rate limit, and not counted against the limit of requests in flight. It is not cached by a policy of its own.

version.description: The Factory release this binary is (`info.version` of this document).

edition.description: The build: `licensed`, or `open` for the open gateway (no licensed code; those routes answer 501 `licensed`).

provider.description: a server setting: `live` calls the providers; `mock` answers every chat and module model call with canned text.

agentProvider.description: a server setting: the same for the agent gateway's pass-through.

catalogFingerprint.description: The SHA-256 of the catalog file this process loaded, in hex, as `sha256sum` prints it; null when no file is set. Processes with the same value run the same catalog.

simSeed.description: Local simulations only: the installed a server setting, as a string. Absent everywhere else.

get.summary: Readiness: whether to send this process traffic (`ready`, `degraded`, `draining` or `unavailable`).
get.description: Outside `/v1`: no credential, no rate limit, and not counted against the limit of requests in flight. `draining` comes first; otherwise a database ping decides, bounded by 2 s. A ping that waits longer than the pool threshold is `degraded`, still 200.

200.description: Send traffic: `ready`, or `degraded` with its reasons.

waitedMs.description: How long the database ping waited.

thresholdMs.description: The wait above which Gateway is degraded.

503.description: Send no traffic: Gateway is stopping (`draining`), or the database ping failed (`database`) or did not answer in time (`database_timeout`).

get.summary: The `nexus` CLI this Gateway serves: its version, SHA-256, download URL and the oldest CLI Gateway talks to.
get.description: Outside `/v1`: no credential. HEAD answers the same headers. Without `target`, it describes the JavaScript bundle (`/cli/nexus.js`); with `target`, the native build for that platform (`/cli/nexus-<target>`). Other methods answer 405 with `Allow: GET,HEAD`.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: A platform, `<os>-<arch>`: lowercase letters and digits, 16 at most each.

200.description: The build to install. `target` is present only when the request named one.

Cache-Control.description: `no-cache`: a client checks again before it reuses the answer.

url.description: Where to download it, on this Gateway's public URL.

minimum.description: a server setting: an older CLI gets 426 `cli_too_old` on `/v1`.

404.description: `cli_target_unavailable`: this Gateway publishes no native build for `target`.

503.description: `cli_bundle_unavailable` (`server_error`): no `target`, and no CLI bundle is built on this Gateway. Also `overloaded` or `draining`, as every route outside the health checks.

post.summary: Start `nexus auth login`: a device code for the CLI and a user code to approve in Nexus UI (ten minutes, single use). No key needed.

client.description: e.g. nexus CLI on <host>. Control characters are dropped. Without agent and scope, each character outside ASCII is stored as ?. A label that starts with an agent's reserved label (Nexus Slack) needs that agent and a scope, else a 400 reserved_client.

agent.description: With scope: the agent the sign-in is for (slack). Its approval issues an agent link (nxo_…), never a personal token.

scope.description: With agent: the matrix actions the agent link holds, space-separated (models.use, spend.read_own, connectors.use, chat.ask, chat.web, agents.memory). Any other is a 400 invalid_scope.

client_id.description: With a server setting: the OAuth client that signs in (nxc_cli). Without one, nxc_unregistered. An unknown or revoked client is a 400 invalid_client.

503.description: `cutover_paused`: only while the operator pauses sign-in for the auth cutover; nothing changed. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

error.message: sign-in, account deletion and organization changes are paused while Nexus moves to its new sign-in; try again after the maintenance window

post.summary: Poll for the device login's token, no faster than `interval`. 400 with code authorization_pending, slow_down (with a new interval), expired_token or access_denied until approved; then a personal token, once, or for a sign-in that asked for a scope, an agent link that holds only that scope. With `grant_type` `authorization_code` (Rust only), the phone's sign-in exchanges the code `authorizeApp` sent to its redirect URI, with its PKCE verifier, for a personal token, once; 400 `invalid_grant` for an unknown, used, expired or mismatched code, which a failed try also uses up.

schema.description: Each grant needs its own fields. A device-code poll (`grant_type` `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`, or none) needs `device_code`. An `authorization_code` exchange needs `code`, `code_verifier` and `redirect_uri`. A missing field is a 400.

device_code.description: The device login's code (`grant_type` `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`, or none).

code.description: With `authorization_code`: the code sent to the app's redirect URI.

code_verifier.description: With `authorization_code`: the PKCE verifier whose S256 challenge `authorizeApp` was given (RFC 7636).

redirect_uri.description: With `authorization_code`: the redirect URI the code was sent to.

scope.description: The matrix actions an agent link holds, space-separated; only for a sign-in that asked for a scope.

ui_url.description: Nexus UI's address , when Gateway knows it: where a client's links into Nexus UI go.

get.summary: Your live tokens in this organization; `?all=1` for everyone's (owners and admins). Newest first; `limit` and `cursor` page it.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor, while more items follow. Only when limit or cursor was sent.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: `1` for everyone's tokens (owners and admins); default: yours

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page, 1 to 500 (default 100). Without limit or cursor the answer holds the whole list.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: nextCursor from the previous page. A cursor whose item left the list answers 400 `invalid_cursor`.

post.summary: Create a personal API key for CI, scripts and the API. The key is in this answer only. A person holds at most 100 live API keys in an organization: the next is refused with 409 `api_key_limit` until one is revoked.

delete.summary: Revoke a token: your own, or anyone's for owners and admins.

post.summary: Revoke a module's scoped key (`nxs_…`) before it expires, without rotating a server setting (owners and admins). A scoped key lives one hour and stops when its person leaves the organization; this stops one key at once. Name it by its key id (`scoped:<product>/<capability>/smk_…`) or by its `smk_…` mint id; 400 `invalid_scoped_key` for anything else. `GET /v1/spend` shows the key id as `keyId` on each model call the key made. The audit log shows it as the actor of the key's connector writes. Gateway keeps no record of the keys it mints, so it accepts any well-formed id. A revoke does not prove that the key was live. Revoking a revoked key answers `already: true` and changes nothing. With `dryRun: true`, nothing changes. Audited as `key.revoked` with target type `scoped_key`.

id.description: The key id (scoped:intelligence/wiki/smk_…) or the mint id (smk_…).

reason.description: Why, kept in the audit event.

dryRun.description: Check the id and change nothing.

get.summary: The organization's service accounts (owners and admins: `service_accounts.manage`), newest first. Each has every key it held, live or not, newest first. Never a token or its hash. `limit` and `cursor` page it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page, 1 to 500 (default 100). Without limit or cursor the answer holds the whole list.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: nextCursor from the previous page. A cursor whose item left the list answers 400 `invalid_cursor`.

post.summary: Make a service account, a caller for CI and scripts (owners and admins: `service_accounts.manage`). A member answers for it (`ownerUserId`, the caller by default) and a team owns it (`team`, its slug or id). It expires at `expiresAt`, at most 365 days from now. An organization holds at most 100 live accounts: the 101st is a 409 `service_account_limit`. It is no member and holds no seat. Its keys (`nxsa_…`) reach the public endpoints only, until a Policy Engine statement admits them to more: every other route answers 403. It has no key until one is issued. Audited as `service_account.created`. With `dryRun: true` everything is checked and nothing is written: the answer is a 200 with the account as it would be made, and its id is never used.

200.description: A dry run: the account as it would be made

400.description: Not valid: no name (1 to 64 characters), an `expiresAt` that is not a future time within 365 days (`invalid_expiry`), an owner who is not a member (`owner_not_a_member`) or a team that is not the organization's (`unknown_team`)

delete.summary: Revoke a service account and every live key it holds, in one change (owners and admins: `service_accounts.manage`). Its keys answer as an unknown token from then on. Revoking a revoked account answers `already: true` and changes nothing. With `?dryRun=1` nothing changes: the answer counts the keys it would stop. Audited as `service_account.revoked`, with the ids of the keys it stopped. Another organization's account is a 404.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: `1` or `true`: check and change nothing. `0` or `false`: the same as none. Any other value is a 400, so a mistyped flag never revokes.

400.description: `dryRun` is not `1`, `true`, `0` or `false`

404.description: No such service account in this organization (`unknown_service_account`)

post.summary: Issue a key for a service account (owners and admins: `service_accounts.manage`). The token (`nxsa_…`) is in this answer, and in a replay of it (same `Idempotency-Key`, within 24 hours), as for `POST /v1/auth/tokens`: Gateway keeps only its hash. The key lives 90 days unless `expiresAt` says otherwise, and never past its account. An account holds at most 5 live keys: the sixth is a 409 `service_account_key_limit`. A revoked or expired account takes no key (409 `service_account_revoked`, `service_account_expired`). Audited as `service_account.key_created`, never with the token.

400.description: No label (1 to 80 characters), or an `expiresAt` that is not a future time within the account's life (`invalid_expiry`)

404.description: No such service account in this organization (`unknown_service_account`)

409.description: The account is revoked or expired, or holds 5 live keys

delete.summary: Revoke one key of a service account (owners and admins: `service_accounts.manage`). The key answers as an unknown token from then on. A key that is already revoked answers as it was, and nothing changes. A key of another service account is a 404. Audited as `service_account.key_revoked`.

404.description: No such key in this service account (`unknown_service_account_key`)

post.summary: Replace a live key with a new one, in one change (owners and admins: `service_accounts.manage`). The old key stops at once. The answer holds the new key and its token, once (a replay with the same `Idempotency-Key` within 24 hours returns it again). The new key keeps the old label unless `label` names another, and lives as long as the old key did unless `expiresAt` says otherwise, never past its account. A key that is revoked or expired does not rotate (409 `key_not_live`). Audited as `service_account.key_rotated`, with the old key as `before` and the new as `after`.

400.description: A label that is not 1 to 80 characters, or an `expiresAt` that is not a future time within the account's life (`invalid_expiry`)

404.description: No such key in this service account, or no such service account (`unknown_service_account_key`, `unknown_service_account`)

409.description: The key is not live (`key_not_live`), or its account is revoked or expired

get.summary: Your live agent links in this organization; `?all=1` for everyone's (owners and admins). Never a token or what it hashes to. Newest first; `limit` and `cursor` page it.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: `1` lists everyone's links. Only owners and admins may: anyone else answers 403 `role_required`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page, 1 to 500 (default 100). Without limit or cursor the answer holds the whole list.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: nextCursor from the previous page. A cursor whose item left the list answers 400 `invalid_cursor`.

403.description: `?all=1` without the organization rung of the keys ladder (`role_required`)

post.summary: Link an agent that acts for you (people only: a service account, a module key or another agent answers 403). `grant` names what it may do: `models.use` (the default), `spend.read_own`, `connectors.use`, `chat.ask` (Ask your code alone, askCode), `chat.web` (web search alone, askWeb) and `agents.memory` (your agent memory alone). The token (`nxo_…`) is in this answer, and again in a repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` within 24 hours: Gateway keeps only its hash. The agent holds that grant cut down to your role now, and none of the routes that are yours alone. The link lives 90 days unless `expiresAt` says otherwise, at most 365. A person holds at most 20 live links in an organization: the next is 409 `agent_link_limit`. Audited as `agent.linked`, never with the token. With `dryRun: true` everything is checked and nothing is written: the answer is a 200 with no token.

200.description: A dry run: the link as it would be made, with no token

400.description: Not valid: an `agent` that is no slug (`invalid_agent`), no label (1 to 80 characters), an empty `grant` (`invalid_grant`), an action that cannot be granted (`grant_not_allowed`) an `expiresAt` that is not a future time within 365 days (`invalid_expiry`), or a field that the body does not define

403.description: The caller may not link: a module key (`module_key`), a service account or another agent (`role_required`), a caller that is no person (`person_required`), a person who is no longer a member (`not_a_member`), or a `grant` that the caller's role does not allow (`role_required`)

409.description: The person already holds 20 live links (`agent_link_limit`)

delete.summary: Unlink an agent: your own link, or anyone's for owners and admins (the keys ladder's organization rung). Its token answers as an unknown token from then on. Your own tokens and your other links do not change. Unlinking an ended link answers as it was and writes nothing. A session link is deleted when it ends, so unlinking it again answers 404. Audited as `agent.unlinked`.

403.description: Another person's link, and the caller is no owner or admin (`role_required`)

404.description: No such link in this organization (`unknown_agent_link`)

get.summary: The OAuth clients you registered for your forks, revoked ones included, oldest first, and the scopes a fork may ask for (`grantableScopes`). People only.

403.description: A caller that is not a person: a service account, a module, a sandbox, an agent link or a third-party token (`person_required` or `role_required`)

post.summary: Register an OAuth client for your fork of a Nexus app. It gets its own `nxc_…` id. `allowedScopes` names what its tokens may hold, each one of `grantableScopes`; without it, all of them. No scope for administration, billing, provider keys, invitations or token management is allowed. People only.

400.description: A blank or too long name, an unknown field, or a scope a third-party client may not hold

403.description: A caller that is not a person: a service account, a module, a sandbox, an agent link or a third-party token (`person_required` or `role_required`)

post.summary: Revoke an OAuth client you registered. `reason` defaults to `revoked by owner`. A revoked client answers as it was: its first time and reason stay. People only.

400.description: A blank or too long reason, or an unknown field

403.description: An official client, which only Nexus's staff revoke, or a caller that is not a person

404.description: No client with this id that you registered (`not_found`)

post.summary: Revoke the calling token. An agent link may end itself whatever its grant.

get.summary: Who the calling credential is, and nothing else: its kind, its organization's id, its person's id, an agent link's grant, and the email only for a person's own credential. Any valid credential may call it (`authenticated`): an agent link and an operator whatever their grant. No organization details, no other member and no role. A person's id is set for a person's own credential, for an agent link (the person it acts for) and for an operator (the operator); a service account, a module key and a sandbox have none. Not audited, as `GET /v1/tenants/me` is not; an operator's request is logged as `operator.request`.

person.summary: A person's own API key or CLI token

agentLink.summary: An agent link that holds only models.use

401.description: No credential (`missing_credential`), or one Gateway does not accept: unknown, expired or revoked (`invalid_credential`).

403.description: An operator grant that is unknown, expired, revoked or another person's (`operator_grant_invalid`).

get.summary: Your organizations: your personal organization first, then each company organization, with your role in each and which one this request is in.

post.summary: Create a company organization that Nexus Gateway alone holds, with no sign-in provider organization behind it. You become its owner. Without a slug, the first free one made from the name is used. Only once the Gateway holds organizations; before that, 409 `use_nexus_ui`. Audited as org.created and member.joined.

name.description: 1 to 120 characters after trimming

slug.description: A lowercase DNS label that is not a Nexus UI page (`settings`, `invite`, …)

org.description: A slug, an id, or personal

post.summary: Delete your own account, from a sign-in made in the last ten minutes (not an API key; a dry run says signInNeeded when yours is older). The sign-in provider deletes your sign-in, the payment provider deletes your personal organization's customer (its plan ends at once), and Gateway takes you out of every organization, closes your personal organization and erases your email and name. Your organizations' spend and audit trail stay, under your user id. Before the customer goes, paying after the fact turns off and one charge tries your personal organization's unpaid usage on the card on file; what it does not collect is written off (unpaidUsageUsd), and its Nexus credits are lost (creditsLostUsd). Refused while you own a company organization: transfer ownership first. A deletion needs confirm: "DELETE", which the person types to confirm. dryRun checks and changes nothing.

confirm.description: What the person typed to confirm: DELETE. A deletion without it changes nothing (400 `confirmation_required`); a dry run needs none.

400.description: The person did not type DELETE to confirm (`confirmation_required`). Nothing changed.

error.message: type DELETE to confirm that you want to delete your account: send "confirm": "DELETE"; nothing was deleted

403.description: A sign-in older than ten minutes (`recent_sign_in_required`): sign in again first. An API key, not a sign-in (`sign_in_required`), or a caller that is no person (`person_required`). Nothing changed.

post.summary: Your heartbeat while Nexus UI is open and visible, about every 30 seconds (every role: `members.read`; a signed-in member only, 403 `role_required` otherwise). You count as online for two minutes after it. Gateway stores at most one every 20 seconds, and none while you turned off showing when you are online. It may carry what you are doing (`activity`): `chatting`, a `page` by id, or `idle`. A change of activity is stored at once. Answers your setting.

You are always online to yourself. `showOnline` is your own setting. Each online member's `activity` says what they are doing, as you may see it.
Whether you show when you are online (every role: `members.read`; a signed-in member only). On unless you turned it off.

Name `emails`, or `pending: true` for everyone in a team by email who has not joined. Emails already in the organization or already invited are skipped. `dryRun` sends nothing. post.summary: Link a GitHub App installation to this organization (owners and admins), with the `state` of its install link; starts Wiki runs for its repositories. When Gateway has the App's OAuth client, the setup redirect's `code` is required and the GitHub user it names must administer every repository of the installation (an owner does, and so does the user account itself): 403 `invalid_code` for a code GitHub refuses, 403 `installer_not_authorized` otherwise. `installerChecked` says whether that check ran.

code.description: The setup redirect's one-time `code`, when the App asks for user authorization on install. Used once to check the installer, never stored.

installerChecked.description: Whether the installer's GitHub identity was checked: false while Gateway has no OAuth client for the App.

400.description: No `installationId`, no `state` (`missing_state`), or a `state` Nexus did not sign (`invalid_state`)

403.description: No owner or admin (`role_required`), another org's `state` (`invalid_state`), or an installer GitHub refuses (`invalid_code`, `installer_not_authorized`)

409.description: This org's install link expired (`invalid_state`), or another org already linked the installation (`installation_taken`)

delete.summary: Unlink an installation and its repositories (owners and admins).

post.summary: Start a Nexus Wiki run on a linked repository now.
GitHub's webhooks for the Nexus GitHub App, verified by X-Hub-Signature-256: installation changes, and pushes to a linked repository's default branch (which re-run its Wiki).

The identity provider's webhook, signed by Svix with a server setting (svix-id, svix-timestamp and svix-signature; refused more than five minutes from now). For organizationMembership.created, .updated and .deleted, and user.deleted, Gateway reads the membership or the person from the identity provider again and makes its copy match: a member the identity provider no longer has loses their membership, teams and tokens (member.removed, via: clerk; the owner loses only the tokens), and a role the identity provider changed is mirrored. For organization.updated, Gateway reads the organization from the identity provider again and mirrors its name, slug and logo as a sign-in does (org.settings_changed, actor clerk; a logo not on img.clerk.com is dropped); an organization Gateway does not have is ignored. A repeated or late event changes nothing. 401 for a bad signature; 503 `not_configured` without a server setting or the identity provider's secret key; 502 when the identity provider does not answer, so Svix retries.

Stripe's webhook, signed by Stripe with a server setting (the Stripe-Signature header, t=<unix>,v1=<hex>; refused more than five minutes from now). Gateway keeps the verified event's identity once in an inbox and nothing else: a repeated delivery changes nothing, and an event whose livemode differs from the key's is kept as ignored. After it answers, Gateway reads the event's object again from Stripe and updates the organization's card on file (`GET /v1/billing`). A signed event Gateway cannot keep (a thin event, no id) is a 200 with `stored: false`, so Stripe does not retry it. An event that stopped (`unmatched`, or failed on its last try) runs again when Stripe sends it again, with all its tries. 400 for a body that is not JSON; 401 `invalid_signature` for a bad or old signature; 413 over 1 MB; 503 `not_configured` until the server settings are both set and well formed. The 503's message says only that Stripe is not configured; Gateway logs the reason at start.

event.description: The event's type. Null when the signed event has no string `type` (or the body is not a JSON object); Stripe's own events always have one.

stored.description: True when this delivery added a row to process. False for a repeat that changes nothing. False too for a resend of a stopped (`dead`) or `unmatched` event: no row is added, but the event runs again from its first try. False for an event whose livemode differs from the key's: it is kept as `ignored` and never processed.

400.description: Not JSON (`invalid_request_error`)

401.description: The signature is bad or too old (`invalid_signature`)

503.description: Stripe is not configured (`not_configured`)

get.summary: The organization's billing (owner only): the Stripe mode of this Gateway, whether the organization has a Stripe customer yet, its payment method on file (`defaultPaymentMethod`, of any type; `paymentMethod` only when it is a card), how it pays for what Nexus runs (pricing v2.0: `freeStart`, `credits` and `autoTopup`, `afterTheFact`; `plan` where this Gateway sells plans), the numbers a page shows (`pricing`), and `pastDue`. `pastDue` is null, or names the oldest month Stripe could not collect: when it first failed (`since`), its period, and when model calls stop (`blockedFrom`, `since` plus a server setting, 7 days by default). From `blockedFrom` until an owner pays, every model call is refused with 402 `payment_past_due`. Never Stripe's customer id or the card number. A customer made in the other mode (test or live) is not shown. 503 `not_configured` until the server settings are both set and well formed (the message says which is wrong).

403.description: Not the owner (`permission_error`)

503.description: Stripe is not configured (`not_configured`): the message says which variable is wrong

get.summary: The organization's bill for one UTC month (owner only). A month the close stored answers from the stored row, as it closed, and `invoice` shows its Stripe invoice. Any other month is priced now, from the ledger and the prices Gateway has: the server settings. Both are 0 until a price is set, so the total reads 0. It counts the calls on the organization's own provider keys. Refused calls and calls a Nexus subsidy paid are left out. Money is a decimal string. The bill is the total in whole cents, rounded down, as a string. `carriedInUsd` is the rest of the newest stored month before this one. `carriedOutUsd` is the part below one cent, and it carries into the next month. A month under 50 cents is not invoiced: all of its total carries. `providerCostUsd` is what the providers charged. They bill it, not Nexus. The stored months are the ones of Gateway's Stripe key mode. Without Stripe nothing is stored, so every month is priced now. The route reads no Stripe, so it answers with Stripe off. 400 for a period that is not YYYY-MM or has not started.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: YYYY-MM from 1970-01 to 9998-12, a UTC month that has started; default the current month

400.description: Not a month as YYYY-MM, or a month that has not started (`invalid_request_error`)

403.description: Not the owner (`permission_error`)

Each month shows its total, its whole cents, its state and its Stripe invoice page. A `closed` month is under 50 cents: nothing was invoiced and its total carries into the next month. Money is a decimal string. The route reads no Stripe. 503 `not_configured` until the server settings are both set and well formed (the message says which is wrong).

post.summary: Start saving a card for the organization (owner only): a link to a card page hosted by Stripe Checkout. Open `url` in a browser before `expiresAt`. Stripe sends the person back to the organization's billing page in Nexus UI (<web app>/<org>/billing?checkout=done` or `=cancelled`). Gateway makes the organization's Stripe customer on the first call and reuses it after; each call makes a new link. Takes no body, or `{"embedded": true}`: the same card setup as a form Nexus UI shows inside its billing page. With a server setting on Gateway, that answer is `EmbeddedCardSetup` (Stripe.js's `clientSecret` and the `publishableKey`, no `url`), and Stripe sends the page to `?checkout=done` once the card is saved; without it, the hosted link as without the body. 400 when `embedded` is not a boolean. Audited as `billing.customer_created` when the customer is made, and as `billing.customer_deleted` when Stripe no longer has it; neither event names Stripe's customer id. 502 `stripe_error` when Stripe refuses or does not answer (the message names Stripe's type and code). 503 `not_configured` until Stripe is set up, or without the web app's address on Gateway; 503 `billing_setup_in_progress` while a first call for the organization is still running (try again in a moment).

post.summary: Confirm a payment the bank wants the cardholder to confirm (3-D Secure), owner only. Off session, Stripe refuses such a charge with `authentication_required` and keeps its PaymentIntent; this confirms that same usage charge after the fact again on session; one the bank's page never finished is cancelled at Stripe an hour later. An auto top-up that turned off for the bank's check is fixed by saving the card again (startPaymentMethodSetup). `status` `redirect`: open `url`, the bank's page, which sends the person back to the organization's billing page in Nexus UI (<web app>/<org>/billing?confirmed=1`). `succeeded` or `processing`: Stripe took it, or a bank debit is on its way. Stripe's notice records the payment as for any charge; nothing is charged twice. Takes no body. 409 `nothing_to_confirm` when no charge waits for the bank's check (save the card again with startPaymentMethodSetup), `charge_running` while a usage charge is being taken. 402 when the card is declined on session.

Stripe sends the person back to the organization's billing page in Nexus UI (<web app>/<org>/billing`). Gateway makes the organization's Stripe customer on the first call and reuses it after; each call makes a new link. Takes no body. The Stripe account needs a default portal configuration. 502 `stripe_error` when Stripe refuses or does not answer (the message names Stripe's type and code). 503 `not_configured` until Stripe is set up, or without the web app's address on Gateway; 503 `billing_setup_in_progress` while a first call for the organization is still running (try again in a moment).

post.summary: Buy Nexus credits (owner only): the organization's own money, prepaid at face value and never expiring, spent by Nexus features after the free start and a plan's included usage at provider price plus Nexus's rate. Body: `amountUsd`, a decimal string in whole cents, from "10.00" to "10000.00"; a new organization buys at most $100 in its first 7 days, counting the purchases still being paid, such as an open Checkout page until it expires (400 `purchase_limit`). With a payment method on file, Gateway charges it off session: `status: credited` with the credits after, or `processing` for a bank debit still on its way (Stripe's notice credits it). Without one, or when the bank wants the person (3-D Secure) or the card declines, `status: checkout` with a Stripe Checkout `url` to open before `expiresAt`; Stripe sends the person back to <web app>/<org>/billing?checkout=credits`. A payment credits once, from Stripe's `payment_intent.succeeded`, and only to the organization whose Stripe customer paid. The Idempotency-Key header keys the Stripe call, so a retry never charges twice. Audited as `credit.purchased`. 400 `invalid_amount`; 502 `stripe_error`; 503 `not_configured` until Stripe is set up, or without the web app's address for a hosted purchase. With paymentToken, charge the agent wallet shared payment token directly in Stripe test mode. Live mode returns 503 payment_tokens_not_supported before contacting Stripe. There is no hosted fallback. 400 invalid_payment_token rejects a malformed credential, or one Stripe has deactivated (used, revoked or expired); 402 payment_authentication_required requires the cardholder. The same Idempotency-Key and body replay the first result.

put.summary: Turn the organization's auto top-up of Nexus credits on or off (owner only). Body: `enabled`, and `belowUsd` and `addUsd` as decimal strings in whole cents (or the ones set before). On needs the payment method on file (409 `no_payment_method`), and not a card whose payment was disputed (409 `card_disputed`). A closed organization cannot turn it on (409 `organization_closed`). When the credits left fall below `belowUsd`, Gateway's Stripe sweep charges that payment method `addUsd` off session and credits it, one top-up at a time, at most 3 top-ups or $500 a UTC day. A decline, a bank that wants the person, no payment method, a bank debit that fails later (`payment_intent.payment_failed`), a dispute, or a refund that takes the credits below zero turns it off, and `offReason` says why. Off keeps the amounts; turning off what was never set answers `autoTopup: null`. Audited as `credit.auto_topup_changed`. 400 `invalid_amount`; 503 `not_configured` until Stripe is set up.

Idempotent: the same file twice changes nothing the second time. `dryRun` returns the same diff and changes nothing; `prune` also removes what the file does not list (never spend). A dry run returns a `plan` (a hash of the diff): apply with `plan` set to it and Gateway refuses (409 `plan_changed`) if the organization changed since, so exactly the reviewed changes apply. An import that would leave more than 2,000 teams in the organization, and adds any, is refused with 409 `team_limit`.

Owners and admins see the organization; members their own usage and their teams', with teammates as one row by person. An agent link sees only its person's own calls, as `person=me` does for anyone. with groupBy=team, `depth` and `under` roll spend up the tree: each group includes its teams below; spend on a team that has child teams, above the depth shown, is its own `(direct)` group. Members see rollups only from their own teams down. With groupBy=key, each key shows by its name and prefix, never its token. A revoked key keeps its name and says revoked. A person's Nexus UI sessions are one group. A member sees the keys of their own calls. All other calls in their teams are one Others row. A member's own call with no key is Unassigned. With groupBy=hour, each group is one UTC hour with calls (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH`), in order, under the same scope as by day; the series stays by day.

post.summary: Ask for an operator grant on a customer's organization (`operator_grants.issue`; the caller must also hold a platform role, else 403 `operator_required`). The grant names a reason, a list of actions and an expiry (24 hours by default, at most 7 days). Each action must be one an admin may do. It must not spend the organization's money or act as one of its people (model and chat calls, the coding-agent gateway, the caller's own keys and tokens, the organization switch, modules and connectors, sharing and reading artifacts, search, device login approval, the operator grants themselves). It must not change, for good, who reaches the organization (members, invitations, email domains, teams, artifact shares outside it), its credentials (provider keys, anyone's API keys and tokens, GitHub installations), its money limits (budgets and spend limits) or its settings (chat retention, artifact sharing limits). A name from either list is a 400 `invalid_scope`. Policy changes (`policy.manage`, `policy.manage_team`) are open to a grant. It makes no member and no seat. The operator then sends its own person token with the header `x-nexus-operator-grant: opg_…`. Audited as `operator_grant.issued` in both organizations. With `dryRun: true` everything is checked and nothing is written: the answer is a 200 with the grant as it would be made, and its id is never used.

get.summary: Search what you may read, grouped by type and ranked: your own chat sessions (titles and message text), artifacts shared with or by you, people, teams, models and model policies.
get.description:
Nexus UI's ⌘K palette and `nexus search`. Every group is filtered on the server by the permission matrix and your role before it is ranked: chats are only ever your own (owners and admins included); people who have not joined yet need `teams.manage`; model policies need `policy.read`; models are those you may use (and coming soon ones). Artifacts follow their audience (`artifacts.read`), and a revoked one is found by its author only. Not searched: the docs and the audit log.

Ranking: the whole query equal to a field scores 1.0, a prefix 0.9 to 0.95, every word starting a word 0.75 to 0.85, the query inside 0.65, every word inside 0.5, scaled by the field's weight (a name 1.0, an email 0.9, teams 0.6). A chat adds recency (15 %) and counts a message match at 0.45 to 0.6. Groups come in the order of their best result. Match ranges are [start, end) in UTF-16 code units.

parameters.description: What to search for, 1 to 200 characters. Words match as prefixes (`depl` finds deploy)

get.summary: The models you may use under your organization's, team's and key's policies (OpenAI-compatible list, with Nexus's fields: each supported model's context window, output limit, reasoning and list prices, enough for a client to offer it without a catalog of its own). Send the key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key: <key>`. **With a key**: `status=allowed` (the default) gives the models you may use; `status=all` the whole catalog with `allowed` and `status`; `supported` or `coming_soon` filter it. `team`: as for a call (else `x-nexus-team`, else your default team). **Without a key** (the public catalog, for the model pages and other readers): the catalog itself, the same for everyone, `supported` models by default and `status=all` or `coming_soon` on request, with no `allowed` field, no `status=allowed` and no `team` (asking for `status=allowed` or a team, by `team` or `x-nexus-team`, is a 401); limited per address, and cacheable (`Cache-Control: public`, `Vary: Authorization, X-Api-Key, X-Nexus-Ui-Secret`). A wrong key is a 401, as on every route.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: With a key: `allowed` (the default), `all`, `supported` or `coming_soon`. Without a key: `supported` (the default), `all` or `coming_soon`; `allowed` needs a key and is a 401 without one.

post.summary: Send a message; the answer streams as server-sent events (OpenAI chat.completion.chunk; `stream: false` answers with JSON). The call takes the same path as /v1/chat/completions: the model policy decision (nexus/auto by default), the ledger's reserve and settle, attribution to you, your team and chat. Ask your code ranks your organization's Nexus Wiki sections (BM25) and cites them. A refusal is stored in the session and answered before any stream: 403 model_not_allowed (naming the level and rule), 402 budget_exceeded or payment_past_due; error.nexus names the session and the stored message. With an Idempotency-Key a message runs at most once; a finished stream is not replayed (409 idempotency_stream_replay). With `images` a question carries up to 8 images, PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP by their bytes, at most 5 MB each and 20 MB in all; `content` may then be empty. They go to the model with the question (and with the next ones while they are among the last two questions that had any) and are stored beside it: the message lists them in `attachments`, and getChatAttachment returns their bytes. 400 invalid_image, 413 image_too_large, 400 model_no_image_input for a model that does not read images.

Restore an old version: the next version gets its title and content. Audited as page.restored.

List a saved Site version’s routes
