get.summary: A version's source as written, as plain text: the HTML, Markdown or JSX to edit and write back with writePageVersion. Use version `latest` for the newest. It is never rendered on the API's origin.

200.description: The source, `text/plain`; the `x-nexus-page-version` header names the version

get.summary: A page's live events, as server-sent events: a version event when a version is written, a preview event when an editor posts unsaved text, and its shared draft's updates, to whoever may open the page. A query event (PageQueryEvent) says one of the page's queries has a new result (Nexus Data).
get.description: Each event is `event: <type>` and one line of JSON `data`: `version` (`PageVersionEvent`), `preview` (`PagePreviewEvent`), the shared draft's `doc` (`PageDocEvent`), and `awareness` (`PageAwarenessEvent`) and `presence` (`PagePresenceEvent`, page presence). Only its owner and editors get `doc` and `awareness`; other readers get `version`, `preview` and `presence`. The first is the page's latest version when the stream opens, then its preview when it has one. A `: keep-alive` comment goes out every 15 s, and the caller's access is checked again then: the stream ends when it is lost (or an editor may now only view the page), or when the Gateway copy is draining. A reader that falls behind is dropped. Reconnect, or poll `getPageVersion`.

404.description: Not a page you may open, or a pinned share (`page_not_found`)

503.description: Too many live readers on this Gateway copy (`page_events_full`): poll instead

get.summary: The page's shared draft: the Yjs updates its editors posted, oldest first, for an editor that joins late. Its owner and the editors of an edit share.
get.description: Gateway stores the updates as opaque bytes and never parses them. Apply `updates` on top of the draft's seed, the source of version `seed`, to get the draft. Empty when nobody has edited since the draft last started over. A snapshot posted with `upTo` set to `last` replaces every update here.

403.description: A reader who may only view the page (`page_read_only`)

404.description: Not a page you may edit (`page_not_found`)

post.summary: Post to the page's shared draft: a Yjs update, a compacted snapshot, an editor's awareness (cursor and name), or their presence.
post.description: An update is stored and relayed to the page's live readers as a `doc` event. A snapshot (`snapshot: true`) replaces the updates up to `upTo` when set, and is not relayed; an editor also posts a change too large for one update this way. An awareness update is relayed as an `awareness` event, and a `presence` object as a `presence` event; neither is stored, and each names its poster as Gateway knows them (`from`). A viewer of the page's latest version may post presence; only an editor posts awareness, updates and snapshots. An update is at most 256 KiB, a snapshot 20 MiB, an awareness update or a presence object 4 KiB. At most 1200 updates, snapshots and awareness posts a minute per person, and 1800 presence posts. Send it without an `Idempotency-Key`: a repeated update changes nothing.

400.description: A malformed body, or a `seed` that is not one of the page's versions

403.description: A reader who may only view the page posted an update or a snapshot (`page_read_only`)

404.description: Not a page you may edit, or for presence, open at its latest version (`page_not_found`)

409.description: The draft started over from a newer version (`page_doc_stale`, `details.seed`): read it again

put.summary: Post the shared draft's text as the page's live preview, so every reader sees an edit before it is saved.
put.description: An editor posts the whole text it holds, built on the page's latest version (`baseVersion`). It replaces the page's one preview, is checked as a version is, and is announced to the page's live readers as a `preview` event. Every reader of a share that follows the latest version, people outside the organization and public links too, then sees it in the page's live frame (`frameArtifact`, `framePublicArtifact`, `framePageVersion` with `live`). Writing a version deletes the preview. It is not a version: it has no history and is not audited. Draft posts and previews share the limit of 1200 a minute per person. Send it without an `Idempotency-Key`: a repeated post changes nothing.

400.description: A malformed body, content a page may not hold (`page_content_blocked`), a `sheet` that breaks its schema (`page_sheet_invalid`, with the first problem at `error.nexus.path`), or a board that does not parse (`page_board_invalid`)

403.description: A reader who may only view the page (`page_read_only`)

404.description: Not a page you may edit (`page_not_found`)

409.description: A version was written since `baseVersion` (`page_preview_stale`, `details.latestVersion`): post the draft built on it

post.summary: Share one of your pages as an artifact, with the same audiences as a chat: the organization, chosen teams or people, or outside it (named people by email, or anyone with the link) as its settings allow. Pin a version, or follow the latest. Sharing again makes a new version of the artifact. Audited as artifact.shared.

get.summary: Where the fast viewer's /a/<page id> takes the caller. The page's owner gets the page's organization, to open /app/<org>/pages/<id>. Anyone else gets the share of the page they may read with the most access, to open /a/<artifactId>. By person: the caller needs no organization. 404 page_not_found when the caller owns no such page and reads no share of it; 403 pages_off.

The comments on a page, oldest first, with whether you own it. Whoever may open the page: its owner, or anyone who may open one of its active shares (a comment is a read: the shares have no comment role). A public link alone is not enough. Anyone else: 404 page_not_found. A reader of a pinned share sees the threads on the versions it shows.

post.summary: Comment on a page: a new thread on a passage (quote, with the text before and after it, on a version) or on a point of a design's board (pin), or a reply (threadId). Whoever may open the page: its owner, or anyone who may open one of its active shares (a comment is a read: the shares have no comment role). A public link alone is not enough. Anyone else: 404 page_not_found. 403 pages_off when the organization turned pages off; 400 page_comment_limit at 1000 comments.

patch.summary: Resolve a thread, or open it again: its first comment, by its author or the page's owner (else 403 page_comment_forbidden).

delete.summary: Delete a comment, by its author or the page's owner (else 403 page_comment_forbidden). A thread's replies go with it. Deleting the page deletes all its comments.

post.summary: Ask Nexus to make the change a thread asks for (the page's owner only, else 403 page_owner_only): opens a new chat of yours that holds the page's latest version, posts a reply in the thread that names the chat, and answers the instruction to send there as your first message. That turn is an ordinary chat turn, billed to you, and its write_page writes the page's next version. Audited as chat.session_created.

Ask Nexus to make the changes several threads ask for, in one chat (the page's owner only, else 403 page_owner_only): the threads threadIds names (a reply names its thread), else every open thread, oldest first. Opens a new chat of yours that holds the page's latest version, posts a reply in each thread that names the chat, and answers one instruction with every comment and its passage or pin. 400 page_comment_none_open when there is none, page_comment_ask_limit above 50 threads, page_comment_ask_too_long when the instruction would pass a chat message's 32000 characters; 404 page_comment_not_found for an id not on the page. That turn is an ordinary chat turn, billed to you. Audited as chat.session_created.

Ask Nexus about one board of a design (the page's owner only, else 403 page_owner_only): regenerate it, make 3 variants of it under it (each data-status="proposed" with data-variant-of and a one-line data-note), or keep a variant in place of its original. Opens a new chat of yours that holds the page's latest version and answers the instruction to send there as its first message, so that turn writes the next version and the one before stays in the versions. 400 when ask or board is malformed (read after the page's access check); 404 page_board_not_found when the latest version has no board with that data-id. That turn is an ordinary chat turn, billed to you. Audited as chat.session_created.

get.summary: Your own preview of a version, or of the page's live state (`live`: its unsaved preview, else its latest version): a signed URL on the sandbox origin, valid five minutes. 503 pages_viewer_unconfigured when this Gateway has no sandbox origin.

get.summary: A small WebP picture of a page version (640 by 400), for the Artifacts library's cards. Only html, jsx and md pages have one; any other format is 404 poster_unavailable. The page checker renders it on the first request, and Gateway stores it; later requests serve the stored bytes. Without a checker, 503 poster_not_configured; a busy checker is 503 poster_busy; a checker that cannot render the page is 404 poster_unavailable; any other failure is 502 poster_failed. To whoever may open the version: its owner, or a reader of one of its active shares; anyone else gets 404 page_not_found. A person only.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: A version number, or `latest`: the newest version the caller may open

get.summary: A page version's data files, by name, without their bytes: read-only copies of the files its source names, attached in the chat that wrote it. To whoever may open the page: its owner, or a reader of one of its active shares; anyone else gets 404 page_not_found. A person only: a public link's reader with no Nexus identity is refused.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version whose files to read: one the caller may open. Default: the newest they may open (a pinned share's version). Another is 404 page_not_found.

get.summary: One of a page version's data files with its bytes, for the page's window.fs.readFile. 404 page_file_not_found when it has none by that name. To whoever may open the page: its owner, or a reader of one of its active shares; anyone else gets 404 page_not_found. A person only: a public link's reader with no Nexus identity is refused.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version whose files to read: one the caller may open. Default: the newest they may open (a pinned share's version). Another is 404 page_not_found.

get.summary: A page's queries (Nexus Data), by name. Its owner reads every field, pending ones included. A reader who is not the owner reads only the approved ones' names, parameters and refresh intervals, never a statement or a connection. To whoever may open the page: its owner, or a reader of one of its active shares; anyone else gets 404 page_not_found. 403 page_queries_off while the organization's artifacts.pages.queries is off (the default). A person only.

put.summary: Save and approve one of your page's queries (Nexus Data): a new one, or a change to one, a pending one included. One SELECT or WITH statement on a connection of postgres or snowflake that you may use, as a call of yours would pick it (403 connection_required, connector_disabled or not_granted otherwise). 503 page_query_unconfigured when this Gateway does not offer the connector. Parameters are declared with a type and bound as $1, $2… when it runs, never spliced into the text; a Snowflake query declares none. 400 page_query_statement_invalid for anything but one SELECT or WITH of at most 100,000 bytes, page_query_connector_unsupported, page_query_params_invalid, page_query_refresh_invalid, page_query_limit past 20 per page. Only the page's owner: 403 page_query_owner_only for a reader, 404 page_not_found for anyone else; 403 page_queries_off while artifacts.pages.queries is off. Audited as page_query.saved, with the statement's SHA-256, never its text. 201 when new, 200 when changed.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The query's name: what the page's code passes to `window.nexus.query`

delete.summary: Remove one of your page's queries, approved or pending. The page's code gets 404 page_query_not_found for it from then on. Only the page's owner: 403 page_query_owner_only for a reader, 404 page_not_found for anyone else; 403 page_queries_off while artifacts.pages.queries is off. Audited as page_query.deleted.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The query's name: what the page's code passes to `window.nexus.query`

post.summary: A page query's result (Nexus Data): the snapshot every reader of the page shares for these parameter values. A run inside the query's refresh interval answers it; past it, Gateway reads it again as the query's approver, one refresh at a time, and announces the new result on the page's events (`query`). The body names parameter values, and `refresh` for the owner's Refresh now: 400 page_query_run_invalid for any other field, page_query_params_invalid for an undeclared name, a missing value or a value of another type. 409 page_query_pending until the owner approves it, 404 page_query_not_found once removed. When the approver left the organization or their access to the connection ended, every snapshot of the query is deleted and the run is refused with the connector call's code (connection_required, connector_disabled, not_granted) or 409 page_query_approver_gone. 503 page_query_unconfigured when this Gateway does not offer the connector. A refresh that fails answers the last rows with `error`, or 502 page_query_failed with none; its message never quotes the database. 429 past 240 runs a minute per person or 2,400 per page. To whoever may open the page: its owner, or a reader of one of its active shares; anyone else gets 404 page_not_found. 403 page_queries_off while artifacts.pages.queries is off. A person only.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The query's name: what the page's code passes to `window.nexus.query`

get.summary: A page version as a file: PNG (one board, at 1x or 2x), SVG (one board, as shapes and text: its box shadows and filters are dropped, and it names its fonts without embedding them), PDF (one page per board, at its size), PPTX (one slide per board), standalone HTML (the page with the canvas, its scripts and fonts inlined) or zip (the PNGs, the HTML and the source). A Nexus Design page's boards are its top-level data-artboard elements. A Nexus Slides deck's boards are its top-level section[data-slide] elements, each at its own size, and its PPTX carries each slide's data-notes as speaker notes by default. Hidden slides are excluded. Any other html or jsx page is one board. Markdown exports as a printable PDF. It renders in the page checker's Chrome; without one, 503 export_not_configured. A board that did not render is named in x-nexus-export-failed (percent-encoded JSON, [{ board, error }]) and the others still export. To whoever may open the version: its owner, or a reader of one of its active shares; anyone else gets 404 page_not_found. A person only.

parameters.name: board
parameters.description: One board or slide, by its data-id, its name or its number from 1. Required for a PNG or SVG of a design or a deck with several (400 board_required); one that matches none is 404 board_not_found.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: The pixel ratio the boards render at. Default: 2 for pdf and pptx, 1 otherwise.

parameters.name: notes
parameters.description: Include speaker notes in deck exports. Defaults to true in PowerPoint and false in PDF.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version to export: one the caller may open. Default: the newest they may open.

200.description: The file, as an attachment; x-nexus-export-failed names the boards that did not render

get.summary: A shared page's frame URL on the sandbox origin, valid five minutes, to anyone who may read the artifact. An unpinned page share's frame shows the page's live state, unsaved edits included; a pinned share's frame shows its version. Frame it with sandbox="allow-scripts" only. 404 artifact_not_found for a shared chat id; 404 artifact_revoked once revoked; 403 pages_off; 503 pages_viewer_unconfigured.

parameters.name: siteVersion
parameters.description: Request signed routes for this exact authorized saved Site version.

get.summary: A shared page's live events, as server-sent events, by the share's id: for readers without the page's own stream (the /a/ viewer, the phone app). Anyone who may frame the share reads it, and it counts no open. A query event (PageQueryEvent) says one of the page's queries has a new result (Nexus Data).
get.description: Each event is `event: <type>` and one line of JSON `data`, as on `streamPageEvents`: `version` (`PageVersionEvent`) and `preview` (`PagePreviewEvent`), never the draft's `doc` or `awareness`. The first is the page's latest version, then its preview when it has one. Reload the share's live frame at each one. The frame URL lasts five minutes, so mint a new one when it is about to expire. The share is checked again every 15 s with a `: keep-alive` comment, and before an event when the last check is a second old: the stream ends once the share is revoked or expires, or the Gateway copy is draining. Do not reconnect after a stream that ends at once.

post.summary: Remix a shared page (its artifact's id, or a public link's token): copy the version it shows into a new page of your own, in the organization you call with, and open a new chat on the copy, so the chat's next write_page writes its version 2. The original page and its shares do not change. Needs your organization's pages on (403 pages_off). A page shared in one of your organizations is remixed there (403 stays_in_organization). From outside the sharer's organization, its artifacts.external.continue must be on (403 external_remix_off). A shared chat id returns 404 artifact_not_found. A shared chat's public token returns 400 not_a_page. Audited as page.created (via remix) and chat.session_created.

get.description: Each event is `event: <type>` and one line of JSON `data`, as on `streamPageEvents`: `version` (`PageVersionEvent`) and `preview` (`PagePreviewEvent`), never the draft's `doc` or `awareness`. The first is the page's latest version, then its preview when it has one. Reload the share's live frame at each one. The frame URL lasts five minutes, so mint a new one when it is about to expire. The share is checked again every 15 s with a `: keep-alive` comment, and before an event when the last check is a second old: the stream ends once the share is revoked or expires, or the Gateway copy is draining. post.summary: Create a skill from a SKILL.md: version 1. Refused with 409 `duplicate_name` when you already have a skill of that name; `error.nexus.skillId` names it. Audited as skill.created.

get.summary: Your skills, most recently written first. A person keeps at most 200.
One of your skills and its versions, newest first. Or a library skill you may load (`listSkillLibrary`), where only the versions an approver approved and did not withdraw exist.

delete.summary: Delete one of your skills, every version and its content, for good. Audited as skill.deleted.

post.summary: Write the next version of one of your skills. With `baseVersion`, refused with 409 `skill_version_conflict` when that is no longer the latest. A new `name` in the front matter renames the skill (409 `duplicate_name` when you have another of that name). Audited as skill.version_written.

get.summary: One version of one of your skills, with its SKILL.md. Or a library skill you may load (`listSkillLibrary`), where only the versions an approver approved and did not withdraw exist; `latest` is the newest approved one. A held, refused or withdrawn version is 404 `skill_version_not_found`, and a library skill you may not load is 404 `skill_not_found`.

A version's SKILL.md exactly as it was written, byte for byte, as `text/markdown` (never rendered on the API's origin). The `ETag` is its SHA-256. A library skill you may load (`listSkillLibrary`) exports at an approved version, and `latest` is the newest approved one.

200.description: The SKILL.md, `text/markdown`; the `x-nexus-skill-version` header names the version

post.summary: Ask to promote one version of one of your skills to the organization or to a team you are in. A copy of the version is held until an approver who is not you approves or refuses it. Your skill stays yours. A repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` within 24 hours gets the first answer and writes no second event. Audited as skill.promotion_requested, and the approvers are told.

400.description: `invalid_promotion`: a field is missing, unknown or out of bounds, `team` goes with `scope` `team` only, or the note is over 500 characters

403.description: `not_in_team`: a team-scope request from someone who is not in the team; the matrix refuses a module key (`module_key`), a service account or an agent link (`role_required`) and an operator (`operator_scope`)

404.description: `skill_not_found`, `skill_version_not_found` or `unknown_team`: no such skill of yours, version, or team

409.description: `personal_org`: a personal organization has no one to approve; `promotion_exists`: this version already has a held or approved promotion to this target (`details` names it and its state); `promotion_limit`: you hold 20 undecided requests, or the organization 200

post.summary: Record that a coding agent's session was delivered some of your skills, for a launcher (`nexus claude`, `nexus codex`). Each skill must be yours, or a library skill you may load (`listSkillLibrary`), and each version must exist and, for a library skill, be approved and not withdrawn (404 `skill_not_found`, `skill_version_not_found`); the record takes the version's name and SHA-256 from what Gateway stores, not from the request, and for a library skill also its scope (`team` or `org`) and the approved promotion that allowed it. The session must be one you opened, of the agent the surface names (404 `session_not_found`). All the records are written, or none (400 `invalid_load` for a request that is not well formed). It says what was delivered, never that the skill ran.

get.summary: The load records of one of your sessions, in the order they were written: which skill and version it loaded in web chat, or was delivered by a launcher. A session that is not yours, and a session with none, answer an empty list.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The chat session (`chs_…`) or the agent session

get.summary: The library skills you may load, at the version a session loads: the highest approved version that nobody withdrew. An organization's library reaches every member, and a team's reaches that team's members and the members of the teams under it. Membership is read at each call, so a person who left a team stops seeing its library at once. The organization's skills come first, then the teams' skills, all by name (not grouped by team). Each skill says whether its name collides with another's (`duplicateName`), so a client that holds your own list too can apply the name rules without the SHA-256 of your skills. It holds no skill text: read a version with `getSkillVersion` or `exportSkill` and the library skill's `id`. A personal organization has no library, and an organization with nothing approved answers an empty list.

403.description: The matrix refuses a module key (`module_key`), a service account or an agent link (`role_required`) and an operator (`operator_scope`). The domain answers any other caller that is no person with `person_required`; the matrix stops each kind first

get.summary: The skill promotion requests you reach, newest request first: your own, those to the teams you lead and the teams under them, and for owners and admins every one. It holds no skill text.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Only promotions to the organization or to a team

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: A team slug or id: only promotions to that team

parameters.name: mine
parameters.description: `true` for the requests you made, whatever else you reach

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Promotions per page, 1 to 200 (default 50). An empty value is no limit

post.summary: Approve or refuse a held promotion. An owner or admin decides for the organization; a lead of the team or of a team above it, an owner or an admin decides for a team. Never the requester, and only from a Nexus UI session or a CLI sign-in, not an API key. An approval adds the version to the library of its scope and tells the requester; a refusal needs a `reason`. Audited as skill.promotion_approved or skill.promotion_refused. A repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` within 24 hours gets the first answer; a repeat without one gets 409 `promotion_decided`.

400.description: `invalid_promotion`: a field is missing, unknown or out of bounds, or a refusal has no `reason`

403.description: `role_required`: only an owner, an admin or a team lead decides; `person_session_required`: an API key cannot decide, run `nexus auth login`; `self_approval`: nobody approves their own request; the matrix refuses a module key (`module_key`), a service account or an agent link (`role_required`) and an operator (`operator_scope`)

404.description: `promotion_not_found`: no such promotion in your reach

409.description: `promotion_decided`: the promotion is no longer held (`details` names its state); `requester_left`: the requester is no longer a member; `team_deleted`: the target team no longer exists; `name_taken`: an approval would give people two library skills of one name (`details` names the scope and team); `library_limit`: the library holds its most skills, or the skill its most versions

post.summary: Withdraw a promotion. The requester withdraws their own held request; an approver who reaches it withdraws a held one, or an approved version (from a Nexus UI session or a CLI sign-in). The version leaves its library; text a model already read stays read. With `allVersions`, every approved version of that library skill is withdrawn in one transaction, each with its own event. The answer names the promotion and, in `withdrawnIds`, every promotion withdrawn. Audited as skill.promotion_withdrawn. The requester is told, unless they withdrew it themselves.

400.description: `invalid_promotion`: a field is unknown or out of bounds, or `allVersions` names a held request

403.description: `person_session_required`: withdrawing an approved version needs a Nexus UI session or a CLI sign-in; `role_required`: the caller asks to withdraw an approved version and is not an approver of it (its requester gets this); the matrix refuses a module key (`module_key`), a service account or an agent link (`role_required`) and an operator (`operator_scope`)

get.summary: Your devices for end-to-end encrypted session sync, oldest first, with their public keys and approvals.
get.description: Revoked devices are listed too. Each approved device names its approver and the approver's Ed25519 signature, so a client verifies the approval chain from your first device itself. `trust` says how this Gateway trusts a device: with `gateway`, a trusted device may have no approver and no chain to verify.

403.description: Not a person: an agent link, a module or a service account (`person_required`)

post.summary: Register a device's or a recovery key's public keys. Your first device is trusted at once; anything later is pending until a trusted device approves it.
post.description: The device makes its own X25519 and Ed25519 key pairs and sends only the public keys, 32 bytes each in base64url without padding. A passkey or recovery code (`kind`) sends its X25519 key only. A device is trusted without an approval only while you never had a trusted device; a recovery key never is. After that, signing in alone never adds a trusted device: the way back after losing every device is `recoverDevice`, with a recovery key's proof. You may have at most 10 pending devices. A Gateway whose `listDevices` answers `trust: gateway` trusts each device at once instead, with no approver, and a device key already pending turns trusted when it registers again. A recovery key stays pending there too.

400.description: A name or key of the wrong form

403.description: Not a person: an agent link, a module or a service account (`person_required`); or a device from Nexus UI while the organization's `webSessionViewer` is off (`web_session_viewer_off`). A recovery key still registers

409.description: 10 pending devices already (`too_many_pending_devices`): approve or revoke one first

post.summary: The way back after every device is lost: with a recovery key's proof, revoke your devices and register this one as a new root.
post.description: Open the challenge from `recoverDeviceChallenge` with your passkey or recovery code and send it with that recovery key's id. Gateway compares it in constant time with the challenge it issued for that recovery key. Only then, in one step, does it revoke each of your devices that is not revoked, delete their copies, register this device as trusted without an approval, and record `devices.recovered` in the audit log. Your recovery keys stay trusted, with their copies: unlock the history with one, then approve it again from this device with `approveDevice`. Without the proof nothing changes. The challenges are tried once, so a wrong proof closes them too.

400.description: A name or key of the wrong form

403.description: No proof (`recovery_proof_required`), a proof that does not match an open challenge for that recovery key: wrong, expired, used or replaced (`invalid_recovery_proof`), or not a person (`person_required`)

post.summary: Challenges sealed to each of your trusted recovery keys, the first step of the way back.
post.description: For each of your trusted recovery keys, Gateway draws 32 random bytes, seals them to that key, and keeps only their SHA-256. Open the one for your passkey or recovery code and send it to `recoverDevice`, with that key's id, within five minutes. New challenges replace the open ones. You are issued them at most 5 times an hour.

403.description: Not a person: an agent link, a module or a service account (`person_required`)

409.description: You have no trusted passkey or recovery code (`no_recovery_key`): your history cannot be recovered, and your devices cannot be reset

429.description: More than 5 challenges in an hour (`too_many_recovery_challenges`)

post.summary: Approve your pending device or recovery key with a trusted device's signature, and store its first locked copies.
post.description: `signature` is the approver's Ed25519 signature, base64url, over the UTF-8 bytes `nexus-device-approval:v1:{deviceId}:{encryptionKey}:{signingKey}` for a device, or `nexus-device-approval:v2:{holderId}:{kind}:{encryptionKey}:` for a recovery key, with the holder's id and keys as `listDevices` shows them. Each of `keys` is a thread you already have, its content key locked to the new holder. In one step the holder becomes trusted and gets its copies; a refusal stores nothing. Store more copies with `putThreadKeys`. A trusted recovery key whose approver is revoked takes a new approval the same way, which replaces the old one: after `recoverDevice`, your new device approves the recovery key it unlocked with.

400.description: A malformed signature, key or handover, a handover for a recovery key, a thread named twice, or more than 1000 keys

403.description: The signature does not verify with the approver's signing key (`invalid_signature`), the approver is a recovery key (`recovery_key_cannot_sign`), or not a person (`person_required`)

404.description: Not your device, or not your thread (`device_not_found`, `thread_not_found`)

409.description: The approver is not trusted (`device_not_trusted`), the holder is not pending and is no recovery key whose approver is revoked (`device_not_pending`), it registered more than 15 minutes ago (`pairing_expired`), or you already have a trusted recovery key of its kind (`recovery_key_exists`)

post.summary: Revoke one of your devices or recovery keys with a trusted device's signature, and delete its locked copies. Revoked is final.
post.description: `signature` is the revoker's Ed25519 signature, base64url, over the UTF-8 bytes `nexus-device-revoke:v1:{deviceId}`. The revoker is the device itself or another of your trusted devices. A revoked device gets no copies again.

400.description: A malformed signature

403.description: The signature does not verify with the revoker's signing key (`invalid_signature`), the revoker is a recovery key (`recovery_key_cannot_sign`), or not a person (`person_required`)

404.description: Not your device (`device_not_found`)

409.description: The revoker is not trusted (`device_not_trusted`), or the device is already revoked (`device_revoked`)

put.summary: Store a thread's locked copies at one key version for your trusted devices, each signed by one of them. A copy already stored is kept, and the answer says which.
put.description: Each copy is the thread's content key, HPKE-sealed by your client to the device's `encryptionKey`; Gateway cannot open it. Each copy carries the Ed25519 signature of your trusted device `senderDeviceId`, so a session without a device key stores nothing. `keyVersion` is a version one of your devices still holds, or one more than the latest to rotate the content key, for instance after you revoke a device: the new version has copies only for the devices you name, which must be trusted. The latest version only goes up, and a revocation never lowers it. Every device must be yours and trusted, and every signature must verify, or nothing is stored. A thread belongs to the first person who stored a copy for it, also after every copy is deleted. Repeating a request changes nothing.

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The thread's id, as its client names it

410.description: The thread was deleted in the session store (`thread_deleted`)

put.summary: Store your thread's content key locked for the organization's current recovery key, signed by one of your trusted devices. A copy already stored is kept, and the answer says so.
put.description: Under the `user_and_org` content policy, your client seals the thread's content key at `keyVersion` to the organization's recovery key (HPKE) once you have confirmed the key's fingerprint, and one of your trusted devices signs `nexus-org-thread-key:v1:{threadId}:{keyVersion}:{orgKeyId}:{lockedKey}` with Ed25519. Gateway cannot open the copy. The copy keeps the thread's person and organization from your credential. `orgKeyId` must be the organization's current key: a copy for a replaced key is refused, and the copies already stored for it stay. `keyVersion` must be a version your devices hold a copy of. A thread with no upload yet joins this organization, as its first upload would. Owners and admins with `synced_sessions.audit` read the copy (`GET /v1/threads/{threadId}/org-keys`); other members never do. Deleting the thread, or your removal from the organization, deletes it.

post.summary: Typed decisions: a batch of requests to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev), each a `state` and its `questions`, answered with typed judgments and probabilities, never text. Metered as one model call: one model policy decision on the `decisions` surface, one reservation of the batch's maximum cost, one settlement on the summed reported input tokens, one spend record. Only decision models serve it, and `nexus/auto` does not resolve here.
post.description:
`requests` holds 1 to 100 requests, sent a few at a time; `state` (a string, an object or an array) and `questions` (`{ <name>: { type, instructions, criteria } }`, `type` one of `choice`, `score`, `noul`) pass through to the model unchanged. `results` holds one entry per request, in order: its `answers`, or an `error` (the model's `status`, 422 when the request did not validate, with the model's reason only then; none when it never answered): one failed request does not fail the batch. Nexus's key answers, and the organization pays: each batch is held and charged on its Nexus balance (subsidy, then credits, then card) at list price plus Nexus's rate, like a model call Nexus pays for. A direct call shows on the bill as product `core`, capability `decisions`; a module's call (its scoped key) as the module's product and capability. An organization has at most 16 of the Gateway's 32 requests to the model in flight; more wait their turn.

Errors: 503 `decisions_not_configured` when the Gateway has no decision model key or no Nexus-paid path to pay with (the endpoint still mounts); 502 `decisions_upstream_failed` when the model answered none of the requests and failed at least one itself (anything but the caller's own 400 or 422: no answer, a refused or throttled Nexus key, a server error; settled first); 403 `model_not_allowed` when policy denies the model (never sent or reserved, recorded as a refused call); 400 `model_not_supported` for a model not served here; 402 `subsidy_exhausted` when the organization has nothing to pay with (no free start, credits or card), `budget_exceeded` or `payment_past_due`.

402.description: The organization has nothing to pay the batch with (`subsidy_exhausted`, the shape a model call returns), the batch's maximum cost is more than the budget left (`budget_exceeded`), or the organization has an unpaid Nexus invoice past its grace (`payment_past_due`). A `budget_exceeded` refusal carries `notified: true` in its details once Gateway has told the refused person and the organization's owners and admins. The details are a BudgetRefusal: each money figure with its exact decimal twin.

parameters.name: x-nexus-team
parameters.description: The team (slug) this batch's spend goes to; you must be in it. Default: your default team.

get.summary: The organization's write grants (owners, admins, leads and members: `policy.read`; not module keys): which module may write through which connector operation (for Nexus Review: robustness/review may github/pull_review, check_run, issue_comment, reaction, resolve_thread; pull_review also covers pull_review_dismiss; pull_ready, pull_merge, pull_edit, pull_state, pull_reviewers and pull_labels each have their own grant, and no other grant covers a merge), who granted each and when, and the write operations that may be granted. A connector write without its grant is refused (403 write_not_granted).

403.description: The credential does not hold `policy.read`. Every person in the organization holds it; a service account or sandbox key does not (`role_required`), nor a scoped module key (`module_key`).

error.message: only the org's owner or admins can read the model policies (organization, teams, coding agents) and test them for yourself (policy.read)

put.summary: Set the write operations of one connector a module may run in this organization (owners and admins: `policy.manage`), in full: the operations not listed are revoked, and an empty list revokes them all. Each grant and each revocation is audited (connector_grant.granted, connector_grant.revoked); a revocation applies from the module's next call. Policy's decide_call reads these grants before every scoped connector call. Each write attempt is audited as connector.write: outcome written; denied with the refusal's code (no grant, a review event other than COMMENT, a thread of another repository); or failed with the error's code and status when an allowed write failed (a rate limit, a timeout). A grant is per organization, module, connector and operation, not per repository: the module scopes repositories itself.

400.description: Not a connector with writes, or not one of its write operations (`invalid_grant`)

error.message: github/merge is not a write operation; the writes are: pull_review, check_run, issue_comment, reaction, resolve_thread, pull_create, pull_ready, pull_merge, pull_edit, pull_state, pull_reviewers, pull_labels

error.message: only the org's owner or admins can grant modules connector writes (policy.manage)

The github connector refuses a `pull_review` whose event is above it (403 `review_event_refused`) on the next call. Nexus Review reads it to choose its event: it requests changes on a failing check and approves a pull request it read in full with none, each only where the level allows. Audited as review_event_setting.changed with the setting before and after.

get.summary: Whether this organization lets a person's confirmed write from chat run, and which connector operations it may run (owners, admins, leads and members: `policy.read`). Each entry must be a connector write Core has. A write of an operation the list does not name is refused (403 `operation_not_allowed`), even with a confirmed record. Off, a chat agent's approval record is not made, confirmed or used, so a record confirmed before stops working too. What an allowed write lets a member's agent do: a `github` write runs as that member's own GitHub account, connected with POST /v1/connections/github/oauth, so GitHub allows it only what it allows the member, and it is refused (403 `connection_required`) while they have none connected; a module's write runs as the Nexus GitHub App. Audited as chat_write_setting.changed with the setting before and after.

On by default; a saved OFF choice restores approval records per call. Your own session or key only (`approvals.decide`): an agent link gets 403 `person_only`.

A `github` write runs as your own GitHub account (POST /v1/connections/github/oauth), never as the Nexus GitHub App: without one connected it is refused (403 `connection_required`). Off, a write needs a record you confirmed. Your own session or key only (`approvals.decide`): no agent link and no operator grant holds it. It keeps the arguments, so the person sees them. It is pending, expires in 30 minutes and allows the call once, after the person confirms it in Nexus (`confirmUrl`). A chat agent's link only (`connectors.use`): any other caller gets 403 `agent_only`. Refused while chat writes are off (`chat_writes_off`) and for an operation the organization's allowlist does not name (`operation_not_allowed`). Audited as policy.approval.requested, with the hash and never the arguments.

post.summary: Send the app's own error and crash reports to the observability store. Each report becomes one `nexus::client_report` line in the Gateway's log, which reaches Cloud Logging with the Gateway's other lines; the Gateway keeps no copy. A report names what failed and where, never content: its fields are a closed set, each one bounded, and its free text (`name`, `message`) is logged redacted, with quoted text, URL paths and queries, emails and anything shaped like a key or token taken out. A stack frame is logged only as a code location (`at <function> (<file>:<line>:<column>)` or `<binary> +0x<offset>`), with every key or token shape taken out; any other frame is logged as `[redacted]`.
post.description: `reports` holds 1 to 20 reports. A report that breaks a bound or carries an unknown field or a control character refuses the whole request with 400 `invalid_report`, so the app drops it rather than sending it again. The line names the organization by its id and never the person.

400.description: A report breaks the contract (`invalid_report`)

403.description: Not one of the organization's people: a service account, a module or a sandbox (`permission_error`)

post.summary: Report one active minute of the caller on an app: the app's window has focus and the person acted in the last minute. The Gateway keeps active minutes per UTC day, organization, person, surface, app, app version and OS, and the last minute per app. Labels come from fixed lists and versions are bounded: no content, path or address is kept.
post.description: Send about once a minute. One heartbeat counts the Gateway's clock minute it arrives in, at most once per organization, person and app, so two windows or a retry count once. Stored only where activity collection is on; off, a valid body answers `recorded: false` and nothing is stored. Unknown fields are ignored. A person only: a key with no person is refused. Six heartbeats a minute per person on each Gateway copy; past that, 429.

200.description: Checked; `recorded` says whether a minute counted

400.description: A value outside its list or pattern (`invalid_heartbeat`)

403.description: Not a person: a service account, a module, an agent link or an operator (`role_required`)

post.summary: Report errors the caller's app caught, with no content: the app, its version and OS, a kind from a fixed list, and a component and a code the app names from its own code. Never a message, a stack, a path or a URL: the pattern refuses spaces, '/', ':' and '@', and the app must not put content in a name. The Gateway counts them per UTC day, organization, person, app, version, OS, kind, component and code, and keeps each person's last 50 per organization.
post.description: `errors` holds 1 to 20 errors. A value outside its list or pattern refuses the whole request with 400 `invalid_client_error`. `occurredAt` more than 5 minutes ahead of the Gateway or more than 7 days old is replaced by the Gateway's now. Stored only with a server setting; off, a valid body answers `recorded: 0` and nothing is stored. Unknown fields are ignored. A person only: a key with no person is refused. Thirty errors a minute per person on each Gateway copy; past that, 429 and nothing of the request is stored.

200.description: Checked; `recorded` says how many were stored

400.description: A value outside its list or pattern (`invalid_client_error`)

403.description: Not a person: a service account, a module, an agent link or an operator (`role_required`)

post.summary: Report artifact frames that failed to load, with no content: the surface, how it failed, the app and browser versions, and the frame's host, the artifact's id and the HTTP status when the app knows them. Never a URL, a path, a share token or free text: each field is a fixed list or a pattern. The Gateway counts each failure in `nexus_gateway_artifact_frame_failures_total`, which holds no identity, and stores nothing. With a server setting it also writes one `nexus::artifact_frame_failure` log line per failure; off, the default, it logs nothing and `accepted` is 0.
post.description: `failures` holds 1 to 10 failures. A value outside its list or pattern refuses the whole request with 400 `invalid_frame_failure`. Unknown fields are ignored. A person only: a key with no person is refused. Thirty failures a minute per person on each Gateway copy; past that, 429 and nothing of the request is logged.

400.description: A value outside its list or pattern (`invalid_frame_failure`)

403.description: Not a person: a service account, a module, an agent link or an operator (`role_required`)

post.summary: Report artifact frames that failed to load from the public share-link viewer: the same body as the signed-in route. No credential; limited per address, one count per request, on the public artifact reads' limit. With logging on, the line carries `org` "public" and no person.

400.description: A value outside its list or pattern (`invalid_frame_failure`)

post.summary: Report that this install of the open-source desktop app was used today: a random install ID, the day, the app version and release channel, the OS, its major and minor version, the CPU type, and how the app reached models. No credential: the app sends it at most once a day, only while its person has "Send usage data" on. Never a prompt, code, path, name or account. With a server setting the Gateway keeps one row per UTC day and install ID for 90 days, then only counts with no install ID; off, the default, it keeps nothing and `accepted` is false. The client's address is never kept with the event.
post.description: A second report of the same day and install keeps the latest versions and adds its modes to the first's. A value outside its list or pattern, or a day outside the last week, refuses the request with 400 `invalid_daily_active`, whether or not the switch is on. Unknown fields are ignored and never kept. Limited per client address, on the public artifact reads' limit.

202.description: Checked; `accepted` says whether it was kept

400.description: A value outside its list or pattern, or a day outside the last week (`invalid_daily_active`)

post.summary: Send feedback, a crash report the person chose to send, or a report on a model's answer (App Review 1.2), to Nexus's team. The Gateway posts one message to the feedback channel in Slack and keeps no copy. The message names the person (name and email) and the organization, so the team can answer, with the app, its version, the OS and the screen. What the person wrote is shown as plain text, so it cannot mention a channel or a person, hide a link, or pass for the Gateway's own lines; names are code spans, and Slack previews no link. A crash shows its redacted name and message and its top frames, as `POST /v1/diagnostics/reports` logs them, and is logged as one `nexus::client_report` line too. A reported answer shows its reason and model, then the answer as plain text, as the app showed it.
post.description: Only a person sends it: at most 5 a person, 30 an organization and 300 in all in ten minutes on each Gateway copy; past that, 429 `feedback_limit`. A message Slack refused uses up no limit, unless Slack refused it for its own rate limit (429). Without a server setting, 503 `not_configured`. When Slack refuses the message or cannot be reached in 5 seconds, 502 `upstream_error`, and the app keeps the person's words so they can try again.

400.description: Feedback that breaks the contract (`invalid_feedback`)

403.description: Not one of the organization's people: a service account, a module or a sandbox (`permission_error`)

502.description: Slack did not take the message (`upstream_error`)

503.description: No feedback channel on this Gateway (`not_configured`)

get.summary: The plans this organization can take, priced as Stripe holds them (owner only): one source for Nexus UI, the desktop app, both CLIs and the phone. A per-seat plan is for companies and any other plan for personal organizations, so only the organization's kind is listed (`audience`). Each plan has its name (the Stripe Product's), `perSeat`, `minSeats`, and per interval `amountUsd` (the price, per seat for a per-seat plan) and `includedUsd` (included usage each month, per seat), as decimal strings. Each plan also has its cloud hours a month per seat (`includedHours`), the price of an hour past them (`hourlyUsd`, a decimal string or null) and the machine sizes it allows (`sizes`). A price Stripe could not give has `amountUsd: null` and a machine-readable `error` (`stripe_error`, `stripe_timeout`, `inactive`, `not_usd`, `interval_mismatch`, `no_fixed_amount`). Cheapest a month first. `current` is the plan the organization's subscription holds. Prices are cached for 10 minutes. 502 `stripe_error` when Stripe gave none of the listed prices; 503 `not_configured` without Stripe or a server setting.

502.description: Stripe gave none of the listed prices (`stripe_error`)

post.summary: Change the organization's plan, interval or seats (owner only). Body: `plan`, `interval`, `seats` for a per-seat plan (one per member, at least its minimum: left out, Gateway counts them), and `dryRun`. A change that costs more a month applies now, and so does monthly to yearly at the same rate a month or more (a yearly price costs its plan's monthly price a month): Stripe prorates it and invoices the difference at once, and the month's included usage grows by the difference at once (live mode, or a server setting). A payment that fails changes nothing (402 `payment_failed`). Any other change (a cheaper plan, fewer seats, yearly to monthly, monthly to a yearly plan that costs less a month) applies at the period's end through a Stripe subscription schedule, shows as `pendingChange` on `GET /v1/billing`, and replaces an earlier pending change; `DELETE` cancels it. `dryRun: true` answers `when`, `at` and `amountDueUsd` (what is invoiced now) and changes nothing. The Idempotency-Key header keys the Stripe call. 400 `unknown_plan`, `plan_not_for_org`, `same_plan`; 409 `no_plan` without a paid plan, `plan_ending` while the plan is cancelled (renew it on Stripe's billing page first); 502 `stripe_error`; 503 `not_configured` until Stripe and a server setting are set.

409.description: No paid plan to change (`no_plan`), or the plan is cancelled, for this period or a later one (`plan_ending`, with `cancelAt` on `GET /v1/billing`)

post.summary: Start a plan for the organization (owner only): a link to a Stripe Checkout page that starts the subscription. Stripe sends the person back to <web app>/<org>/billing?checkout=plan`, or `=plan_cancelled`. The plans are the ones in a server setting (Pro, Max's tiers, Team, Team Premium), billed monthly or yearly; a per-seat plan has one seat per member, at least its minimum (the seats follow the members), so `seats` may be left out and, when given, must be that number. The plan's included usage is granted once a month as a Nexus subsidy and does not roll over. A per-seat plan is for companies and any other plan for personal organizations (`GET /v1/billing/plans` lists an organization's). 400 `unknown_plan` for a plan or interval this Gateway does not sell; 400 `plan_not_for_org` for a plan of the other kind of organization; 409 `plan_active` while the organization has a live subscription: change it with `POST /v1/billing/plan/change`. 502 `stripe_error` when Stripe refuses or does not answer. 503 `not_configured` until Stripe and a server setting are set, or without the web app's address.

post.summary: Start a Slack install: Slack's authorize URL and the install's id. The URL's `state` names this organization, you, the install and an expiry an hour away, and Gateway accepts it for one completion only. (GitHub's install `state` names only the organization and an expiry, and works again within the hour.) Open the URL in the browser where you are signed in to Nexus UI and approve the app in Slack. Nexus UI then completes the install (`completeSlackInstall`) and you confirm it (`confirmSlackInstall`). People only: an agent link, a service account or a module key answers 403 `person_required`. Writes nothing.

post.summary: Finish an install from Slack's redirect, as the signed-in person: Nexus UI's install page sends the `code` and `state` it received. The `state` must verify, name this install, and name your organization and you; otherwise 403 (`invalid_state`, `not_installer`) and Gateway calls Slack for nothing, keeps no token and writes no binding. This is the login-CSRF guard: Slack's redirect lands in the browser of whoever approved the app, so someone else's install link approved by you lands in your session, not theirs. Then Gateway exchanges the code with Slack's `oauth.v2.access`, seals the bot token in the vault and writes the binding as `pending`, with the Slack user who approved (`approvedBySlackUser`). Audited as `chat_workspace.installed`. Confirm it next (`confirmSlackInstall`); a pending install declined or left past its `state`'s expiry is uninstalled from Slack and its token deleted.

post.summary: Confirm a pending install: the workspace is bound to this organization. Only the person who started and completed the install confirms it, before its `state` expires. A confirmed install answers as it is. A workspace bound to another organization is a 409 `installation_taken`, and this install is revoked with its token. An older binding of the same workspace here is replaced, and its bound channels move to this binding with their teams (`chat_channel.moved`). Audited as `chat_workspace.confirmed`.

404.description: No such install in this organization (`install_not_found`)

get.summary: Slack's redirect after an admin approves the app (`redirect_uri`). It checks the `state`'s signature and expiry, then answers 303 to Nexus UI's install page (the web app's address, which ends in `/app`, + `/settings/slack/installed`) with `code` and `state`. It exchanges nothing and writes nothing: it has no session, so it cannot tell who approved in Slack. Nexus UI finishes the install with `completeSlackInstall`, as the signed-in person. A missing, forged or expired `state` is 403 `invalid_state`; a cancel in Slack is 400 `install_denied`; without the web app's address it is 503 `ui_not_configured`, because an install completes only in a signed-in browser.

parameters.name: error

(A pending install whose workspace is also active here shares that binding's token, so it is revoked without the uninstall.) Then the binding is revoked, with any pending install of the same workspace here, and the bot token leaves the vault. Audited as `chat_workspace.revoked` (`reason`: `unbound` or `declined`) and `connector_credential.revoked`.

post.description: The Gateway cannot reach a desktop app, so the app collects its own push deliveries. The answer holds at most 50, oldest first. Each is handed over once: a second call does not answer it again, and the inbox keeps every item. A delivery older than a day, one whose recipient lost access to it, and one whose group has push turned off are not answered. A device that is not a desktop answers 409 `not_collected`.

post.summary: A piece of a voice-mode answer, said by ElevenLabs: the app plays the `audio/mpeg` it answers, and Nexus's own key stays on the Gateway.
post.description:
Send one piece of an answer, up to 500 characters: a few sentences, about 30 seconds of speech. Split a longer answer at sentence ends and ask for each piece in turn. The model and the voice are the Gateway's. A person may ask for 30 pieces a minute and an organization 300. Where Nexus pays, each piece is charged as AI Nexus runs: ElevenLabs' price for its characters, from the free start and the other grants, then the credits and the card at that price plus 5%, within the budgets. The apps count about 900 characters as a voice minute.

Errors: 400 `invalid_voice_speech` for an empty, blank or longer text; 402 `voice_minutes_used_up` when the budget or the Nexus balance does not cover the piece, so the app answers with the device's voice; 402 `payment_past_due` when the bill is unpaid past its grace; 503 `voice_speech_not_configured` when the Gateway has no ElevenLabs key (the endpoint still mounts), so the app keeps its own speech engine; 502 `voice_upstream_failed` when ElevenLabs refused or did not answer.

post.summary: A short-lived token for dictation: the app's microphone button streams audio to AssemblyAI's speech to text with it, and Nexus's own key stays on the Gateway.
post.description:
Open the WebSocket in `url` (the token is already in it) within `expiresInSeconds`, then send the microphone's audio as binary frames: 16 kHz, 16-bit little-endian mono PCM, about 50 ms each (1,600 bytes). AssemblyAI answers with JSON messages: `Begin`, then a `Turn` for each stretch of speech (`transcript`, `end_of_turn`, `turn_is_formatted`), then `Termination`. Send `{"type":"Terminate"}` to end a session. One session runs at most `maxSessionSeconds`; a longer dictation asks for a new token. The token opens one session.

Errors: 503 `voice_not_configured` when the Gateway has no AssemblyAI key (the endpoint still mounts); 502 `voice_upstream_failed` when AssemblyAI refused or did not answer.

No key: a signed-out visitor calls it. `enabled` is true when this guest id has rounds and output tokens left and its client address has not used today's rounds. A spent guest budget shows only on the next round (429 `guest_chat_paused`). `model` is the display name of the model every guest round runs on.

Errors: 400 `guest_request_invalid` when `X-Nexus-Guest` is missing or not a UUID; 429 `rate_limited` when one address sends too many guest requests; 503 `guest_chat_not_configured` when the Gateway has no guest organization or no Turnstile secret. The endpoint still mounts.

parameters.description: The browser's guest id: a random UUID it keeps (in localStorage). Its rounds count under it.

post.summary: One guest chat round: the answer streams as server-sent events, as sendChatMessage streams it, on the guest model, billed to the guest organization. Nothing of the chat is stored.
post.description:
No key: a signed-out visitor calls it. The body is the whole conversation the browser holds, its last message the guest's (`user`): at most 20 messages and 32,000 characters in all, none empty. `turnstile` is a Cloudflare Turnstile token, checked at Cloudflare before anything counts. The model is always the guest model; a request names none. A round is one accepted request: it counts once the model call starts. A guest id gets a limited number of rounds and output tokens, and a client address a limited number of rounds per UTC day. All guests share a daily spend budget. The stream is sendChatMessage's (`ChatStreamChunk`): a first chunk with the role and `nexus.mode` and `nexus.requested`, a chunk per piece of text, a last chunk with `finish_reason` and `usage`, or an `{error}` event, then `data: [DONE]`. It carries no `nexus.session`, `nexus.question` or `nexus.message`.

Errors: 400 `guest_request_invalid` (a missing or bad `X-Nexus-Guest`, or a body outside the bounds above); 400 `turnstile_failed` (Cloudflare refused the token); 429 `guest_rounds_used` (this guest id used its rounds or its output tokens); 429 `guest_address_limit` (this address used today's rounds); 429 `guest_chat_paused` (the guest budget cannot hold this round); 429 `rate_limited` (too many guest requests from one address); 502 `turnstile_unavailable` (Cloudflare did not answer in 5 s); 503 `guest_chat_not_configured`. A refusal counts no round.

put.summary: Turn paying after the fact on or off, or change its monthly usage limit (owner only; pricing v2.0). Body: `enabled`, and `limitUsd` as a decimal string in whole cents. Turning it on needs the payment method on file (409 `no_payment_method`), and so does turning it on again with no `limitUsd`; a call with `limitUsd` changes the limit of a setting already on without one. A closed organization cannot turn it on (409 `organization_closed`). Calls the free start and the credits cannot pay then go on the card, at provider price plus Nexus's rate, up to the limit in a UTC month (past it, 402 `usage_limit_reached`). Gateway's Stripe sweep charges the card off session each time the unpaid usage reaches `pricing.thresholdUsd` (less carries over, and what is left is charged once it is turned off); a charge that fails stops the calls the card pays (402 `payment_failed`) and tells the owners, until a charge goes through. A disputed payment (`charge.dispute.created`) stops its card the same way (`failed.reason`: `disputed`) until an owner adds another card, and that card never pays again (409 `card_disputed` on turning it on with that card, or on again with no `limitUsd`; a limit change still works). Off stops new calls on the card and still charges what is owed. Off with `limitUsd` keeps the limit, even when it was never on. Audited as `billing.after_the_fact_changed`. 400 `invalid_amount`; 503 `not_configured` until Stripe is set up.

An owner or admin with `synced_sessions.audit` reads any thread of this organization, not deleted; each read is recorded in the audit log as `synced_session.audit_read` before it is served. post.summary: Upload a thread's next sealed events. A retried upload changes nothing, and the answer names the last event stored.
post.description: Events are numbered from 0, with no gap. The request's events are consecutive, and the first is at most one past the last stored. An event already stored must be sent unchanged; the rest are added. All or nothing. The first upload makes the thread yours, in this organization. A new sealed event names the thread's latest content key version, which must already have locked copies (`PUT /v1/threads/{threadId}/keys`): after a rotation, re-seal unconfirmed events with the new key. Your synced threads in one organization hold at most 1 GiB. Usage numbers are stored, not billed. While the organization's effective `sessionContent` is `never`, a new event with a sealed body is refused with 409 `content_policy_never`; usage-only events pass, and events already stored, sent again unchanged, still confirm.

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The thread's sync id, as its runner names it (a UUIDv7)

403.description: Not a person: an agent link, a module or a service account (`person_required`)

404.description: Another person's thread, or yours in another organization (`thread_not_found`)

409.description: The first event is past the next number (`seq_gap`), an event already stored differs (`event_conflict`), the thread has no locked keys yet (`thread_keys_missing`), a key version has no copies (`key_version_not_stored`), or a new event is not sealed with the thread's latest key version (`key_version_behind`): re-seal it with the new key; or a new event carries a sealed body while the organization's content policy is `never` (`content_policy_never`): send usage only

get.summary: One of your threads, live: its new event numbers and its deletion, as server-sent events.
get.description: Each event is `event: <type>` and one line of JSON `data`. `thread` (`SyncedThreadAdvanced`) says the thread now holds every event up to `lastSeq`: read the ones after your last with `listSyncedEvents`. `presence` (`SyncedThreadPresence`) is one watcher's place on the thread, yours included: post yours with `postSyncedThreadPresence`. `deleted` (`SyncedThreadGone`) is the last event. With `commands=true`, the thread's person, with `sessions.control`, also gets `commands` (`CodeCommandsLive`) first, then `command` (`CodeCommandChanged`) when one of the thread's Code commands is queued, claimed, completed or rejected: read its receipt with `getCodeCommand`. A teammate gets neither. No event carries a body. Open the stream with `after`, the last event number you hold: when the thread holds more, `thread` comes at once, so a reconnect misses nothing. A `: keep-alive` comment goes out every 15 s, and your token and the thread are checked again then: the stream ends when either is lost, when you fall behind, or when the Gateway copy is draining. Reconnect with `after`. The thread's person opens it, and so does any member on a team-visible thread while the organization's `multiplayerSessions` is on; an auditor alone does not. A thread made private, or a teammate removed, ends a teammate's stream at the next keep-alive.

parameters.description: The thread's sync id, as its runner names it (a UUIDv7)

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The last event number you hold; -1 (the default) when you hold none

parameters.name: commands
parameters.description: Also send phone control's `commands` and `command` events, when you are the thread's person with `sessions.control`. False by default.

400.description: A malformed `after` or `commands`, or an `after` below -1

post.summary: Tell a thread's watchers where you are on it: the event number on screen, or that you left.
post.description: Gateway relays it as a `presence` event (`SyncedThreadPresence`) on the thread's stream, to its owner's runner and every watcher, you included, and never stores it. Gateway names you; the body names only your window (`client`) and the event number on screen. Post it when you open the thread, every few seconds while it shows, and with `leave` when you close it. A watcher not heard from for a few posts is gone. You may post on a thread you may stream: your own, or a team-visible one while the organization's `multiplayerSessions` is on. Your posts share the pages' presence limit, 1,800 a minute per person on each Gateway copy.

put.description: The organization makes the X25519 key pair in its own vault and sends only the public key. Gateway never holds the private half, so it cannot open a copy locked to it. Replacing the key keeps the old one as revoked, with its history. The same key again changes nothing and records nothing. Once a key exists, the sessionContent setting accepts user_and_org.

403.description: Without synced_sessions.manage_policy (`role_required`), or not a person: an agent link, a module or a service account (`person_required`)

get.summary: The organization's current recovery key: the public half runners lock thread content keys to under the user_and_org content policy, with its fingerprint. key is null until one is registered.
get.description: Every member reads it, so runners fetch it here. Gateway's copy is not the source of trust: before a member's clients lock for this key, the member confirms its fingerprint once against one the organization publishes from its vault (an admin's screen, its wiki or chat), and again after each replacement.

get.summary: Which members lock their synced threads for the organization's current recovery key: each member with synced threads, those with no copy for the key first.
get.description: A member's clients lock for the key only after the member confirms its fingerprint, so `confirmed: false` means they have not, or have not synced since. Counts only: no thread id and no content. `keyId` is null, and `members` empty, until the organization registers a key.

403.description: Without `synced_sessions.audit` (`role_required`)

get.summary: The team key's newest epoch, current or retired, and your holder's copies of every epoch when `holder` names one.
get.description: The team key is the X25519 pair every member's trusted holders hold, so a teammate's device opens a team-visible session. It is not the organization's recovery key. Gateway holds its public half and copies sealed to each holder, and opens neither. `retiredAt` set means a removal or a revoke retired the epoch: make the next one (`POST /v1/orgs/team-key`).

parameters.name: holder
parameters.description: One of your trusted holders: its copies come back

post.summary: Make the team key's next epoch, with its first copies for members' trusted holders. One epoch at a time; audited as org.team_key_rotated.
post.description: Your trusted device makes the X25519 pair and sends its public half and copies of its private half, each sealed to a member's trusted holder and signed. Gateway takes one new epoch at a time, under a lock on the organization: of two devices that race, one makes the epoch and the other gets 409 `team_key_epoch_taken`. A new epoch follows a removal or a revoke: while the newest is current, 409 `team_key_current`. A removed member's holder gets no copy. The audit event names the reason the previous epoch retired, or `first`.

409.description: The epoch is taken (`team_key_epoch_taken`); the newest epoch is current (`team_key_current`); or the sender or a holder is pending or revoked (`device_not_trusted`)

409.description: The sender holds no copy of an epoch it hands over (`team_key_not_held`), or the sender or a holder is pending or revoked (`device_not_trusted`)

Gateway reads the issue and the repository at its default branch through the GitHub connector, runs the coding agent in a cloud sandbox, and opens a pull request that closes the issue with `github/pull_create`. The organization must have agent writes on with `github.pull_create` on its allowlist, and the person their own agents' writes on; otherwise the run fails with `write_not_granted`, `chat_writes_off` or `operation_not_allowed` and opens nothing. get.summary: Read the project's setup: the current version's script, or null when the repository's own committed `.agents/setup` runs, and whether a cloud machine verified it (`unknown`, `verifying`, `ok` or `failed`, with the version and commit the last finished verification ran on). Anyone in the project reads it. 404 project_not_found when you are not in it. Behind a server setting: off, a 404. No agent link and no operator grant holds `projects.use`. 503 not_configured when Gateway has no database.

List the project's saved setup versions, newest first, without their scripts. Anyone in the project reads them. 404 project_not_found when you are not in it. Behind a server setting: off, a 404. No agent link and no operator grant holds `projects.use`. 503 not_configured when Gateway has no database.

post.summary: Save the next version of the project's setup script. It wins over the repository's `.agents/setup`, and the status goes back to `unknown`. Versions are never changed or deleted. A script is 1 to 65536 bytes (400 setup_script_invalid); at most 500 versions (409 setup_version_limit). Audited as `project.setup_saved`. A project admin only (403 project_admin_required), never while it is archived (409 project_archived). Behind a server setting: off, a 404. No agent link and no operator grant holds `projects.use`. 503 not_configured when Gateway has no database.

A cloud machine's host reports a verification of the project's current setup, with the machine's own Nexus token (403 not_machine_token for any other). The machine's owner must be in the project (404 project_not_found). The report names the version it ran; 409 setup_version_stale when that is not the current one. `ok` and `failed` name the commit (400 setup_commit_invalid). 503 cloud_unavailable without cloud machines. Behind a server setting: off, a 404. 503 not_configured when Gateway has no database.

Ask your agent, the one `@nexus` is in Slack. `stream: true`, or `Accept: text/event-stream`, streams the answer as server-sent events: `started`, `model`, `text` (each `delta`), `step`, then `done` or `error`. Gateway forwards it to the agent API with your own token, after its own authentication and rate limit; only a person's credential or their agent link may call it. Off unless the Gateway turns the agent proxy on.
