apiKey.description: A Nexus token (nx_…): a personal API key, a `nexus auth login` token or a Nexus UI session. Modules receive scoped keys (nxs_…) that can call models and connectors only. A service account's key (nxsa_…) holds the public endpoints only.

apiKeyHeader.name: x-api-key
apiKeyHeader.description: The same Nexus token as `apiKey`, sent in the `x-api-key` header instead of `Authorization: Bearer`.

subject.description: A team's slug, a user id or a key id. Ignored for `organization`.

models.description: Required for a `limit` or an `override`; not allowed for a `pause`.

expiresAt.description: An ISO 8601 time in the future.

keyId.description: The key id, when the request named it.

already.description: It was revoked before this request.

ServiceAccountScope.description: What a key reaches, which is its account's. Read from the account when the key is shown, never stored on the key.

teamId.description: The team that owns the account. Its keys stop when the team is deleted.

ServiceAccountKey.description: A service account's key. Never the token, except in the answer that issues or rotates it, and its replays.

ownerUserId.description: The member who answers for its account, as the account holds it now. The key stops when they leave the organization.

prefix.description: The first characters of the token, to recognise it in a list.

lastUsedAt.description: When the key last authenticated, written at most once an hour.

rotatedFrom.description: The key this one replaced in a rotation.

ServiceAccount.description: A caller for CI and scripts. It is no member and holds no seat.

ownerUserId.description: The member who answers for it. Its keys stop when they leave the organization.

teamId.description: The team that owns it. Its keys stop when the team is deleted.

keys.description: Every key it held, newest first.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor, while more items follow. Only when limit or cursor was sent.

ownerUserId.description: The member who answers for it. The caller by default.

team.description: The team that owns it: its slug or id.

expiresAt.description: In the future, at most 365 days from now.

dryRun.description: A dry run's id is never used.

label.description: Required to issue a key. A rotation keeps the old label when it names none.

expiresAt.description: In the future and not past the account's own expiry. 90 days from now by default, or the account's expiry if that comes first. A rotation keeps the old key's lifetime by default.

token.description: `nxsa_…`. In this answer, and in a replay of it (same `Idempotency-Key`) within 24 hours.

already.description: It was revoked before this request.

keysRevoked.description: The live keys it stopped (with `dryRun`, the ones it would stop).

type.description: The class of the error: invalid_request_error (400, 405, 408, 409, 413, 422, 426), authentication_error (401), billing_error (402), permission_error (403), not_found (404), rate_limit_error (429), or a 5xx type such as server_error.

code.description: Stable: branch on it, not on message. Every 4xx carries one: its site's own code, else the default for its status (400 invalid_request, 401 unauthenticated, 402 payment_required, 403 forbidden, 404 not_found, 405 method_not_allowed, 408 request_timeout, 409 conflict, 422 unprocessable, 429 rate_limited, any other 4xx invalid_request). A 502 carries its site's code, else upstream_error. Any other 5xx carries one only when its site sets it. The agent routes (/v1/anthropic/, /v1/openai/) answer in the provider's shape.

param.description: `model` when the error is a model refusal (a `code` starting with `model_`); absent otherwise.

nexus.description: Details of the error, when it has any: the policy rule of a model refusal, the seconds of a 408.

minimum.description: On a 426 `cli_too_old` only: the oldest `nexus` CLI version Gateway supports.

AnthropicError.description: An error on /v1/anthropic/, in the shape of Anthropic's API.

type.description: Follows the status, as in Anthropic's API: invalid_request_error (400), authentication_error (401), billing_error (402), permission_error (403), not_found_error (404), request_too_large (413), rate_limit_error (429); else Gateway's type, such as timeout_error (504) or api_error.

nexus.description: Gateway's stable `code`, plus any details. A details-only error has `code: null`.

OpenAiError.description: An error on /v1/openai/, in the shape of OpenAI's API.

type.description: Follows the status, as in OpenAI's API: invalid_request_error (400, 401, 404), insufficient_quota (402), permission_error (403), rate_limit_error (429); else Gateway's type, such as server_error (504) or api_error.

code.description: Gateway's stable code; else the type.

param.description: `model` for a model refusal; else null.

nexus.description: Gateway's details of the error, when it has any.

ProviderError.description: An agent gateway error, in the provider's shape: Anthropic's on /v1/anthropic/, OpenAI's on /v1/openai/. An error the provider answers passes through as the provider wrote it.

personal.description: Your personal organization, made with the company organization

scope.description: Who holds the key: a team or a person. Absent for the organization's own.

scopeId.description: The team's or the person's id.

state.description: What the provider answered when the key was checked on add: a model listing, which costs nothing. Absent for a key stored before the check. An add the provider rejects answers 400 `provider_key_rejected` and stores nothing. `disabled` and `removed` are an admin's: no call opens such a key. The list marks a disabled key `unused` and leaves a removed one out. `rejected` on a stored key: its provider refused it on a call with HTTP 401; `enableProviderKey` checks it again, and a replacement clears it.

lastUsedOn.description: The UTC day a call last used the key.

versions.description: Each key stored for the provider, oldest first, at most 50; only on `getProviderKey`.

version.description: 1 for the first key stored for the provider, then one more for each replacement.

addedBy.description: The user who added it; absent for Core's own work and for a key stored before Nexus recorded who added keys.

changed.description: False when the key was already in the state asked for, so nothing was written.

providerKey.description: The key after the change, or as it would be after a dry run.

role.description: `developer` is taken as `system`. Answers are always `assistant`.

content.description: The text, or OpenAI's content parts: `{type: "text", text}` (joined) and, in a person's message, `{type: "image_url", image_url: {url}}` with a `data:` URL (Gateway fetches no URLs). An assistant turn that only calls tools may leave it out or send null. Answers carry a string.

tool_calls.description: The tools an assistant turn called (in an answer: when `finish_reason` is `tool_calls`).

tool_call_id.description: A `tool` message: the call it answers.

max_tokens.description: At most the lower of the deployment's cap and the model's `max_output_tokens`; above it is a 400 `output_over_limit` before anything is reserved, with `error.nexus.limit`. A call skips a host whose output limit is below it; when no host it may use takes it, the same 400 names the largest limit of those hosts. A call also skips a host that does not read the call's images (400 `model_no_image_input` when no host does) and a host that does not take its `reasoning_effort` (400 `reasoning_effort_not_offered`). A host whose own context window may be too small for the prompt and `max_tokens` is tried after the hosts that surely hold them. Absent: the model's chat default, within that cap.

stream.description: Answer as server-sent events (`ChatCompletionChunk`). Absent or null: no stream. A value that is not a boolean is a 400 (`stream must be true or false`).

stream_options.description: Accepted for compatibility; a stream always ends with its usage chunk.

tools.description: Functions the model may call, in OpenAI's shape; translated for Anthropic models.

parameters.description: A JSON Schema; `{"type": "object"}` when left out.

tool_choice.description: `auto` (the default), `none`, `required`, or one function by name (it must be in `tools`). `required` or a function on a model that does not take a forced choice is 400 `tool_choice_not_offered`, before anything is reserved.

parallel_tool_calls.description: `false`: at most one tool call per answer.

reasoning_effort.description: One of the model's `reasoning.efforts` (GET /v1/models). Absent: the provider's default. An effort the model does not offer is a 400 `reasoning_effort_not_offered` before anything is reserved; `error.nexus.offered` lists the model's efforts.

response_format.description: OpenAI's `response_format`, sent on as written when the model offers its `type` (`text`, `json_object` or `json_schema`). A type the model does not offer is a 400 `response_format_not_offered` before anything is reserved; `error.nexus.offered` lists the model's types.

finish_reason.description: stop, length, or refusal when the provider declined to answer; its words are in nexus.refusal.

nexus.description: What the call cost and who it was attributed to.

funded_by.description: Who paid the provider. own_key: the organization's own key; nexus_key: Nexus's own key, for Nexus's own organizations; nexus_subsidy: a Nexus subsidy; nexus_credit: the organization's prepaid Nexus credits, charged the cost plus Nexus's rate; nexus_invoiced: an organization under contract, billed the cost plus Nexus's rate on its month's invoice. Unset on the mock provider

refusal.description: The provider's words when it declined to answer (a safety refusal); set exactly when finish_reason is "refusal". Billed as the provider billed it.

router.description: The auto router's pick, on an answer it routed or a chat session held. The answer also carries the header x-nexus-router with the version. Unset on every other answer. The pick's cost estimates stay on the spend record.

version.description: The router version that acted, e.g. auto-v0.0.1.

class.description: The request's class. Unset on a held pick.

reason.description: Why the version chose its model. Unset on a held pick.

held.description: The chat session held its model, with no router run.

default_model.description: The model nexus/auto resolves to for the caller with no router.

effort.description: The reasoning effort the call ran at: the request's own reasoning_effort, else the one the router version picked. Unset when the call ran at the model's default.

budgetUsd.description: The organization's budget, a cap per budgetPeriod. Owners and admins only: a member gets none of budgetUsd, spentUsd, reservedUsd, budgetPeriod and periodSpentUsd. Deprecated: read `budgetUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

budgetUsdDecimal.description: `budgetUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `budgetUsd`.

spentUsd.description: The organization's spend since it began. Owners and admins only. Deprecated: read `spentUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

spentUsdDecimal.description: `spentUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `spentUsd`.

reservedUsd.description: Held by the organization's calls in flight. Owners and admins only. Deprecated: read `reservedUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

reservedUsdDecimal.description: `reservedUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `reservedUsd`.

budgetPeriod.description: Owners and admins only: the budget's period

periodSpentUsd.description: Owners and admins only: the spend of calls reserved in the budget's current period, what the budget counts. Deprecated: read `periodSpentUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

periodSpentUsdDecimal.description: `periodSpentUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `periodSpentUsd`.

remainingUsd.description: Owners and admins: what the organization's budget has left this period. Everyone else: what is left for them, the least room of the organization, their team's caps and their monthly limit, as the next 402 says it. Deprecated: read `remainingUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

remainingUsdDecimal.description: `remainingUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `remainingUsd`.

period.description: Not owners and admins: the period of the cap that binds remainingUsd (`2026-10-17`, `2026-W43` or `2026-10`). For the organization's budget, its current period

resetsAt.description: When the binding cap's period ends and remainingUsd comes back; for owners and admins, when the budget's period ends

scope.description: `org`: the whole organization's calls (owners and admins); `own`: only the caller's

costUsd.description: Deprecated: read `costUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

costUsdDecimal.description: `costUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `costUsd`.

recent.description: Recent calls. fundedBy says who paid the provider (own_key, nexus_key for Nexus's own organizations, nexus_subsidy, nexus_credit for the organization's prepaid credits, or nexus_invoiced for a contract's invoice); unset on refusals, typed decisions and calls from before it was recorded. A call a Nexus subsidy paid also has fundingOrg, the organization whose stored key paid it. A call Nexus paid the provider for (nexus_key or nexus_subsidy) also has markupBps, Nexus's rate on it in basis points (500 is 5%), as it was when the call settled; costUsd stays the provider's cost. A call a Nexus subsidy paid also has subsidyMarkupBps, the rate the subsidy was charged at: the subsidy spent costUsd plus that rate. It is unset on older calls, which spent costUsd alone. An Anthropic call also has inferenceGeo (us or global), where the provider said it ran; unset on other providers and on calls from before it was recorded. Each call also names the caller's key, never its secret: keyId (a token id `key_…`; a module's scoped key id `scoped:<product>/<capability>/smk_…`, which POST /v1/auth/scoped-keys/revoke takes; an agent's link id `agl_…`, so a call of the agent differs from the person's own; `ui`; or a system caller's name) and keyKind (the audit log's actor kind: `api_key`, `cli`, `ui`, `module`, `service`, `sandbox`, `operator`, `agent` or `system`). Both are unset on calls from before they were recorded: an unknown key Each call's `costUsd`, and its `overspendPrevented.limitUsd` and `overUsd`, also come as exact decimal strings: `costUsdDecimal`, `limitUsdDecimal` and `overUsdDecimal`. The numbers are deprecated.

subsidizedUsd.description: Organizations with a Nexus subsidy: what calls the subsidy paid cost the subsidy, each at its provider cost plus Nexus's rate (in your scope: a member gets what it paid for their own calls). Deprecated: read `subsidizedUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

subsidizedUsdDecimal.description: `subsidizedUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `subsidizedUsd`.

subsidy.description: Owners and admins only: the organization's Nexus subsidy (a personal organization's starting credit), funded by Nexus, never the organization's own money. A member's answer has none of it

grantedUsd.description: Deprecated: read `grantedUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

grantedUsdDecimal.description: `grantedUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `grantedUsd`.

spentUsd.description: What settled calls cost the subsidy: each call's provider cost plus Nexus's rate, as for credits. Deprecated: read `spentUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

spentUsdDecimal.description: `spentUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `spentUsd`.

reservedUsd.description: Deprecated: read `reservedUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

reservedUsdDecimal.description: `reservedUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `reservedUsd`.

remainingUsd.description: Deprecated: read `remainingUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

remainingUsdDecimal.description: `remainingUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `remainingUsd`.

expiredUsd.description: What was left of the free start when it expired, 30 days after its grant (pricing v2.0). Absent before. Deprecated: read `expiredUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

expiredUsdDecimal.description: `expiredUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `expiredUsd`.

usableForModelCalls.description: Whether this Gateway pays a Nexus feature's model calls (chat sessions, module runs; never raw model access) of an organization with no key of its own from the subsidy (a server setting, and a server setting's stored keys or a subsidy environment key)

subsidiesPaid.description: The funding organization, owners and admins: what its stored provider keys paid for other organizations' subsidized calls. Never part of its own spend, budget or limits

usd.description: Deprecated: read `usdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

usdDecimal.description: `usd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `usd`.

credits.description: Owners and admins: the organization's prepaid Nexus credits, its own money, never expiring, once it bought some. A Nexus feature's call spends them after the subsidy, at its provider cost plus `markupBps`. Decimal dollar strings.

spentUsd.description: What settled calls cost the credits: each call's provider cost plus `markupBps`.

remainingUsd.description: Bought, less spent, held and reversed. Below zero after a refund or a lost dispute took back credit that was already spent: then Nexus pays for no call (the free start, credits or the card after the fact) until a purchase pays it back.

reversedUsd.description: What refunds, lost disputes and operators took back, and what an open dispute holds of its purchase until it closes. A refund that fails gives its credit back. Only while something is taken back.

markupBps.description: Nexus's rate in basis points (500 is 5%).

payAfterTheFact.description: Owners and admins (pricing v2.0): the organization pays after the fact, so calls the free start and the credits cannot pay still run on its card.

nexusPays.description: Every member: whether Nexus can pay for the organization's next model call, and why not. It reads the payers in the ledger's order: a contract, the free start, other Nexus grants, the credits, then the card when it pays after the fact; an unpaid invoice past its grace stops all of them. It answers for a small call to a model the free start pays for, so a pricier model or a larger call can still be refused. Absent where Nexus pays for no model calls on this Gateway.

payer.description: Who pays the next call; null when `pays` is false

reason.description: Why Nexus cannot pay; null when `pays` is true. `billing_off`: nothing was set up to pay (no free start, no credits, and the card does not pay after the fact). `card_disputed`: a payment on the card was disputed, and only another card pays. `past_due` comes first, also under a contract. A balance under a cent does not count as paying.

changesAt.description: The next time this changes by itself: the free start's deadline while it pays, or the next month while the usage limit is reached; else null

limitUsedPercent.description: While the card pays: how much of this UTC month's usage limit it paid, in whole percent, rounded down. Null while another payer pays, or nobody, and always null for a caller who sees only their own spend: only billing managers see it. Absent from an older Gateway.

coverage.description: Coverage of the codebase: the share of the repository's files in scope that the run's pages cite (Nexus Wiki's GLOSSARY.md). Absent for runs that did not count it.

imageUrl.description: The organization's logo, as the identity provider serves it (https://img.clerk.com/…); unset when it has none.

mark.description: Set only when it is Nexus's own; unset for a customer's.
Set only when it is Nexus's own; unset for a customer's.

user.description: The person calling, when the key is a person's

features.description: The products this Gateway has on. Unset reads as all off.

wiki.description: Nexus Wiki is on. Off, its routes and Ask your code answer 404 wiki_off, and clients hide them.

apps.description: Nexus Apps: `nexus apps` and /v1/apps. An older Gateway leaves it out: off.

agentSessionAudit.description: Coding agent sessions write agent_session.started and agent_session.ended audit events. An older Gateway leaves it out: off.

GatewayFeatures.description: The products a Gateway can turn off. Clients hide what is off.

AgentId.description: A coding agent's id. It names the agent in sessions, policies and routes. Its command may differ: `antigravity` runs as `nexus agy`.

agent.description: The agent to start; auto on a stop of an agent auto request

version.description: The auto router version that chose

reason.description: plan_at_floor, plan_below_floor, paid_at_floor, paid_below_floor or pinned; for stop: no_classifier, no_offer or pinned_unavailable

model.description: Canonical model id

providerModel.description: The id to start the agent with

account.description: The plan account handle the request named

via.description: nexus: every model call through Gateway's agent gateway; subscription: the person's own plan (Claude Code on their Claude login, Codex on their ChatGPT login), calls straight to the vendor, usage as the agent reported it; ori: sessions from before the agent gateway

access.description: Who pays its model calls, as Gateway classified the session when it opened: subscription (the person's own plan), byok (the organization's own provider key, through Gateway) or nexus (Nexus's own key, for Nexus's own organizations; Nexus credit no longer pays an agent). Absent for ori, for sessions from before, and when no key would pay (Gateway refuses those calls).

agentSessionId.description: The agent's own conversation id: `nexus claude --resume <id>` or `nexus codex resume <id>` picks it up again.

usage.description: subscription sessions, once the agent has reported: its calls summed. estimatedCostUsd is the list-price estimate of the priced calls (Claude Code's own, the catalog's for Codex), never charged; unpricedCalls counts the calls with no estimate

unpricedCalls.description: Calls with no estimate, because the agent stated no cost or the call names no model the catalog lists

agentSubscriptions.description: Whether the organization allows subscription routes (GET/PUT /v1/orgs/settings)

install.description: How to install the agent (the vendor's own package; Nexus never installs it)

route.description: The route it takes when the person names none

from.description: Why: the person's preference, the default (gateway), or the organization (subscriptions turned off while the person prefers one)

preference.description: The person's saved route; absent when none

access.description: Who pays on this route: byok (the organization's own key), nexus (a key Nexus pays for) or subscription (the person's plan); null on gateway when no key would pay

available.description: Whether the route can run now; reason says why not

reason.description: Why it cannot, and the command that fixes it

plan.description: subscription: the plan it runs on

login.description: subscription: how to sign the agent in to the plan, once, on the person's machine

loginStatus.description: subscription: how to check that sign-in

spend.description: What the calls metered to this session cost (refused calls left out); zero without calls.

kind.description: `person`: a person's own API key, CLI token or Nexus UI session; `agent_link`: an agent link (`nxo_…`); `service_account`: `nxsa_…`; `module`: a module's scoped key; `sandbox`: a sandbox session's reference; `operator`: a Nexus operator under a grant.

tenantId.description: The organization the credential acts in.

userId.description: The person: the caller's own, an agent link's person, or the operator. Absent for a service account, a module key and a sandbox.

email.description: The person's email, only for a person's own credential.

grant.description: An agent link's granted actions (matrix names). Absent for every other kind.

role.description: The person's role in the organization: the caller's own, or the role of the person an agent link acts for. Absent for every other kind.

features.description: The products this Gateway has on. Unset reads as all off.

AgentLink.description: An agent link as its person sees it. Never the token, and never what it hashes to.

userId.description: The person the agent acts for.

agent.description: What the agent is, as a slug (`slack`).

grant.description: The grant the agent holds: what the person granted, cut to what a link may hold now (`models.use`). The person's role limits it again at each call.

prefix.description: The first characters of the token, to recognise it in a list.

lastUsedAt.description: When the link last authenticated, written at most once an hour.

DeveloperClient.description: An OAuth client as its author sees it.

allowedScopes.description: The actions a token of this client may hold: the client's own list, or every third-party scope when it has none.

grantableScopes.description: The scopes a fork may ask for, in their canonical order.

allowedScopes.description: Each one of `grantableScopes`. Omitted: all of them.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor, while more items follow. Only when limit or cursor was sent.

agent.description: What the agent is, as a slug (`slack`).

grant.description: What the agent may do. `models.use` by default.

expiresAt.description: In the future, at most 365 days from now. 90 days from now by default.

session.description: A link for one agent session: deleted, not kept, when it ends (`DELETE /v1/agent-links/{id}`), so a second end answers 404. It also ends after 15 to 30 minutes without use, so the link of a client that stopped without ending it does not stay live; the client makes a new one. Making one also deletes up to 20 of your ended session links. The audit keeps their history.

token.description: `nxo_…`. In this answer, and again in a repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` within 24 hours. None with `dryRun`.

dryRun.description: The link was not written. Its id is never used.

TeamRole.description: `lead` is reserved for the planned team-lead role and grants nothing extra yet.

parentId.description: The parent team's id; absent for a top-level team.

level.description: The organization's own label for the team's level (e.g. department).

pending.description: People added by email who have not joined the organization yet.

path.description: The team's ancestors, top level first; the last is its parent.

amountUsd.description: The cap for the period; 0 refuses every call. The cap for the period in US dollars: a JSON number (deprecated) or a decimal string with at most 6 decimals (`"12.245"`), read exactly. Send `amountUsdDecimal` instead to send only a string.

amountUsdDecimal.description: The cap for the period as a decimal string in US dollars, at most 6 decimals, never below 0; read exactly into micro-dollars, never through a float. With `amountUsd` too, both must name the same amount (400 `amount_mismatch`).

period.description: UTC calendar day, ISO week (from Monday) or month

mode.description: Only `hard_stop` is available; the others answer 400 `mode_not_available`

warnAtPercent.description: For mode `warn`, which is not available yet

dryRun.description: Check the cap and answer what would change; change nothing

days.description: Every day from `from` to `to`, oldest first; a day without agent calls has no people. Each day also counts its active engineers by product: the people with at least one non-refused call that day, and for `agents` the people with only subscription sessions too. A day with no such person has `engineers` 0 and no products.

subscription.description: People with `subscription` sessions that day (their own Claude or ChatGPT plan) and no agent call through Gateway. A session counts when it reports its first model call. A person on both routes that day is in `people` only. Gateway keeps these counts for 367 days; days before Gateway counted them have none.

engineers.description: Distinct active engineers that day over every product: a person with at least one non-refused call, or with a subscription session for agents.

products.description: Active engineers by product slug (`core`, `agents`, `chat`), sorted by product, only products with someone. A person counts once per product, so these can add up to more than `engineers`. For `agents` the subscription-only people count too.

scope.description: `org`: the whole organization (owners and admins); `member`: your own usage and that of your teams and the teams under them; `own`: only your own calls (an agent link, or `person=me`).

spentUsd.description: Deprecated: read `spentUsdDecimal`, the exact decimal string (root rule 9).

spentUsdDecimal.description: `spentUsd` as an exact decimal string in US dollars with six decimals (`"12.245000"`), from the micro-dollars. Prefer it to `spentUsd`. `null` for a total, group or day with no call at all (root rule 9's empty day), where `spentUsd` is 0.

callsByStatus.description: Calls by status, refused calls included. `calls` counts settled, failed and released calls only.

errorRate.description: (failed + refused) / (settled + failed + refused), 0-1. Released calls count in neither part. `null` when there are no such calls.

overspendPrevented.description: The refused calls a spend limit stopped in the period, and what they asked to hold (`amountMicros` of the record's `overspendPrevented`, not what they would have cost), in all and by the level whose limit refused them. A refusal at a level other than these four counts nowhere. Zeros, not `null`, when no limit stopped a call. It equals the spend file's rows with an `overspendLevel` over the same days.

key.description: Team id, user id, model, provider, product/capability, key id or day; `ui:<user id>` for a person's Nexus UI sessions; `unassigned` for no team (or person, or key); `others` for a member's teammates (or their keys).

ModelRule.description: A model access rule. Patterns: an exact model (`anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`, any spelling), a provider (`anthropic/*`) or a family (`openai/gpt-6-*`). No allow list (or an empty one): every model the levels above allow. A deny wins at any level. Coming-soon models may be named (accepted with a note; no effect until supported).

defaults.description: What `nexus/auto` and `nexus/default` resolve to, per kind; the most specific level that names one wins. Must be supported and allowed by this rule's own lists.

maxPrice.description: Refuses a model priced above either limit, in USD per million tokens. A price equal to the limit passes. A side left out has no limit. A model with no price is refused. Applies at every level, and a lower level only narrows.

denyCountries.description: Refuses a model whose maker country or provider country is listed. Countries are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, listed one by one. A model with no catalog entry is refused when a side is listed. Applies at every level, and a lower level only narrows.

providers.description: Which providers calls may use, by catalog provider id (`GET /v1/providers`). A provider in `deny` is off. With `allow`, only the providers it lists are on, so a provider added to the catalog later stays off until it is listed. Without either, every provider is on. A provider in both lists is off: `deny` wins. An empty `allow` is refused with 400 `providers_allow_empty`: omit `allow` to allow every provider. A model whose providers are all off is refused with 403 `provider_disabled`, and is not `allowed` in `GET /v1/models`. Set on the organization's policy only. An unknown id is refused with 400 `unknown_provider`.

custom.description: False: no rule at this level

migrated.description: Read from the old agent policy, not saved since

effective.description: What the levels down to this one allow, and the defaults they resolve to

model.description: Canonical id of the model that runs (or would)

owned_by.description: The maker: who made the model, the first part of its id

provider.description: Supported models: the host that serves it, whose rules price it and whose key pays for it

context_window.description: Supported models: input and output tokens together, at most

web_search_usd.description: One hosted web search's list price in US dollars, set when the model can run a chat's web search; absent otherwise

max_output_tokens.description: Supported models: the longest output, which Core reserves when a call names no limit. It holds on the agents' pass-through (`/v1/anthropic`, `/v1/openai`); the chat paths cap output at the deployment's limit (a server setting, 4,096 by default): `/v1/chat/completions` refuses a larger `max_tokens` with a 400, and Nexus chat answers within it, except rounds that offer the `write_page` tool, which ask for up to 16,384 tokens within the model's own limit

mode.description: How a call steers it: an effort level (`efforts`), a token budget (Anthropic extended thinking, `budget_tokens`), or not at all (the model does not reason)

efforts.description: The values the provider's effort setting takes (Anthropic `output_config.effort`, OpenAI `reasoning.effort`), lowest first; empty unless `mode` is `effort`

default_effort.description: The provider's default effort; null where the provider states none

can_disable.description: Whether a call may turn reasoning off with the provider's own switch (Anthropic `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`, OpenAI `reasoning.effort: "none"`), at some effort at least: see `disable_max_effort`

disable_max_effort.description: The highest effort at which `can_disable` holds (Claude Opus 5 and Claude Haiku 5.5: `high`); null when it holds at every effort, or `can_disable` is false

pricing.description: List prices Core meters with, per million tokens (supported models). An OpenAI model's `cache_write` sizes a call's reservation, but settlement does not charge it yet

cache_write.description: Cache writes (Anthropic: 5-minute writes; 0 where the provider does not price them)

long_context.description: The rates above `above` input tokens, where the model has a long-context tier

cache_write.description: Cache writes (Anthropic: 5-minute writes; 0 where the provider does not price them)

openWeights.description: Catalog classification. True means open weights. Null means unclassified.

clientSecret.description: The session's client secret: Stripe.js mounts the form with it (`createEmbeddedCheckoutPage`). It opens only this session's form.

publishableKey.description: Gateway's a server setting (`pk_test_…` or `pk_live_…`, the same mode as its secret key), for `loadStripe`.

expiresAt.description: When Stripe stops accepting the form.

url.description: Stripe's customer portal for the organization. Open it at once: it expires within minutes.

NexusCredits.description: The organization's prepaid Nexus credits, its own money, never expiring. A Nexus feature's call spends them after the free start, at its provider cost plus `markupBps`. Decimal dollar strings.

spentUsd.description: What settled calls cost the credits: each call's provider cost plus `markupBps`.

remainingUsd.description: Bought, less spent, held and reversed. Below zero after a refund or a lost dispute took back credit that was already spent: then Nexus pays for no call (the free start, credits or the card after the fact) until a purchase pays it back.

reversedUsd.description: What refunds, lost disputes and operators took back, and what an open dispute holds of its purchase until it closes. A refund that fails gives its credit back. Only while something is taken back.

markupBps.description: Nexus's rate on AI in basis points (500 is 5%).

paymentToken.description: Optional Stripe shared payment token from an agent wallet, scoped to Nexus, USD, the purchase amount and an expiry. Currently accepted only in Stripe test mode. Confirms without a saved card, the web app's address or Checkout. Never accepts card details or merchant API keys. Does not save a card or enable recurring charges.

amountUsd.description: Dollars in whole cents, such as "50.00": from 10.00 to 10000.00.

status.description: `credited`: charged and credited now; `processing`: Stripe is still taking a bank debit, and its notice credits it; `checkout`: open `url` to pay.

amountUsd.description: What the purchase buys, in decimal dollars.

expiresAt.description: When Stripe stops accepting `url`.

checkoutSessionId.description: Exact Checkout session to confirm; returned by current Gateways.

AutoTopup.description: The organization's auto top-up of Nexus credits. Decimal dollar strings.

belowUsd.description: A top-up starts when the credits left fall below this.

offReason.description: Why Gateway turned it off; null while it is on, or after an owner turned it off. `refunded`: a credit purchase was refunded, or a refund took the credits below zero.

todayCount.description: Top-ups charged this UTC day: at most 3.

todayUsd.description: What they bought: at most $500 a day.

pending.description: A top-up is being charged, or Stripe is still taking its payment.

belowUsd.description: Dollars in whole cents, above 0.00 and at most 10000.00. Needed to turn on the first time.

addUsd.description: Dollars in whole cents, from 10.00 to 500.00. Needed to turn on the first time.

autoTopup.description: The setting after; null after turning off what was never set.

module.description: The module whose verb runs, as `<product>/<capability>` (`intelligence/wiki`): the path of the verb's own route.

input.description: The verb's input; `{}` when left out. The organization's owners and admins can read it, so do not put secrets in it.

team.description: The team the job's model calls go to, by slug or id; the caller's default team when left out.

teamId.description: The team the job's model calls go to; absent when its creator is in none.

result.description: What the verb answered; set once the job is `done` or `failed`.

sessionId.description: The desktop session the machine is for; null on a machine made before sessions.

title.description: The session's title, on one line; null when the create sent none.

name.description: The session's title, cut to 120 characters, or `Cloud`.

size.description: Nexus chooses it: a server setting when made.

state.description: The desktop's `CloudState`. `queued` waits for a place, the person's next start or the provider; nothing runs. Running time is charged in `creating`, `starting` and `ready`.

sleepingSince.description: When it went to sleep; null unless `sleeping`.

stopReason.description: Why Gateway put it to sleep: `budget` when its compute was refused, `max_run` after its longest run with no interaction (24 hours by default, from the person's last interaction, create, wake or access), `not_enabled` when the organization may no longer run machines, `idle` when nobody needs it (its agent idle 5 minutes and its person idle 20 minutes, or its host silent 15 minutes, or no report from its host in the 5 minutes after its last create, wake, access or connect), `resize` while it restarts one size bigger after it ran out of memory. Null otherwise, and cleared by a wake.

queuedUntil.description: While `queued`: the earliest time Gateway tries to start it (the person's next start, the provider's `nextStartAt`, or the meter's next pass). Null otherwise.

hostOnline.description: The machine's host has its control connection open on this copy of Gateway: GET /v1/cloud/machines/{id}/connect can open a stream.

repo.description: The GitHub repository, `owner/name` (a github.com URL also works). Required for now.

projectId.description: Reserved for projects: refused for now (`project_id_unsupported`).

agent.description: A coding agent that runs in cloud sessions: `claude` or `codex`, and `opencode` when the Gateway turns it on. Absent, empty or `auto`: the model picks it (open-weight models run on `opencode`, Anthropic models on `claude`, OpenAI models on `codex`). Another agent is refused with `invalid_agent`.

model.description: A catalog model (`GET /v1/models`) or the agent's own model name; absent for the agent's default. Required when `agent` is absent. With `agent`, a catalog model that another agent runs is refused with `agent_model_mismatch`.

prompt.description: The session's first message, 1 to 100000 characters.

title.description: The session's title, kept on one line, at most 200 characters.

idempotencyKey.description: Names the session: a resend with the same body answers the same session. Else the `Idempotency-Key` header's.

id.description: A user id (yours, for `person`), an assistant conversation's id, a room's id, or a session of yours (`cs_…`).

SessionStartedBy.description: Who started a session. Absent on a start: you (`person`).

agent.description: `claude` or `codex`: a cloud session launches only these two agents today.

model.description: The agent's model name; null for its default.

title.description: The session's title; null when the start sent none.

state.description: `starting`: the machine boots or sets the repository up, or the prompt waits for its host. `running`: the agent started. `stopped` and `failed` are final.

threadId.description: The session's id on its machine once the agent started (`t_<uuid>`).

error.description: Why it failed, or why the last message may not have reached it.

machine.description: Its cloud machine; null once the machine is deleted.

fencingToken.description: The session's current fencing token: 0 until a runner first takes it, then raised by one on each take.

runner.description: The runner that took the session last, and its lease; null until one takes it.

runnerId.description: The runner, as it named itself when it took the session.

fencingToken.description: The token the runner holds. Its connector writes inside the session send it in `x-nexus-fencing-token`.

leaseExpiresAt.description: When the lease ends unless the runner renews it. After it, another runner may take the session without `seenToken`.

runnerId.description: Who takes the session: a name of the runner's own, such as its device id.

seenToken.description: The session's `fencingToken` as you read it: take the session over from its holder (a handoff) while that is still its token.

fencingToken.description: The token the runner got when it took the session.

name.description: The server's name for your list. Gateway keeps its first line, cut to 120 characters.

sessionId.description: The desktop session the machine is for (`t_<uuid>`). One live machine for each session. An older app sends none, and gets a new machine each time.

title.description: The session's title. Gateway keeps its first line, cut to 200 characters.

name.description: Read and ignored: the machine's name is the session's title.

size.description: Read and ignored: Nexus sizes every machine.

repo.description: The repository the session clones: a URL, or a GitHub `owner/name`. With a server setting on, a GitHub one starts the machine from the organization's saved copy of it, when there is one and GitHub lets the person read it (`x-nexus-github-token`). Anything else is ignored.

busy.description: Whether an agent on the machine works now. A permission prompt counts as idle.

agentIdleSince.description: Since when every agent is idle; null while one works or before the first.

interactedAt.description: The person's last interaction with the machine's sessions; null when there is none.

oomKills.description: How many processes the kernel killed for want of memory since the machine started (its cgroup's `oom_kill`, else the system's).

grant.description: The sealed grant from the machine's `cloud.json` (`setup.grant`). It holds no credential.

repo.description: The repository the machine sets up (`owner/name`).

token.description: A GitHub App token that may only read `repo`, for an hour at most. Keep it in memory only.

ended.description: True: the grant ended, and no setup token is given for the machine again.

publicKey.description: One SSH public key line, such as `ssh-ed25519 AAAA…`.

hostKey.description: The machine's SSH host key, to pin.

expiresAt.description: When the link stops working; null when it lasts until the machine sleeps.

key.description: A provider key that may only read and stop this machine; null when the provider refused.

apiUrl.description: The provider API the key calls.

providerId.description: The machine's id at the provider.

expiresAt.description: When Gateway deletes the sandbox.

size.description: One of a server setting; `small` when absent.

labels.description: Keys of 1 to 64 characters, not starting with `nexus.`.

exitCode.description: Null when the command was killed (a timeout or a signal).

stdoutTruncated.description: The provider cut stdout: its text is not complete.

stderrTruncated.description: The provider cut stderr: its text is not complete.

path.description: Relative to the sandbox's home, with no `..`.

grantedBy.description: The user id of who granted it

grantable.description: The write operations that may be granted, by connector

actions.description: What the module now holds for this connector

level.description: `comment`: COMMENT only. `request_changes`: COMMENT and REQUEST_CHANGES. `full`: COMMENT, REQUEST_CHANGES and APPROVE.
`comment`: COMMENT only. `request_changes`: COMMENT and REQUEST_CHANGES. `full`: COMMENT, REQUEST_CHANGES and APPROVE.

SpendCall.description: One model call, as the ledger recorded it. Every field is always present, and an unknown value is null. People and teams are named by id only; their names are in the directory file (`exportDirectoryCsv`). Money is a decimal string in US dollars with six decimals. A CSV file has one column per field, in this order.

at.description: When the ledger recorded the call.

status.description: `settled`, `failed`, `refused` (Nexus Gateway refused it, and no money moved) or `released` (its reservation closed without a settle, by a job's cleanup or the ledger's age sweep).

model.description: The model the call asked for; null for a released call, whose model the ledger did not record.

provider.description: The provider that served it; null for a refused or released call, which no provider served.

product.description: The product it is metered to: `core` for direct API calls, `agents`, `chat` or a module.

userId.description: The person who made the call.

teamId.description: The team the call was attributed to; null for none (`unassigned`).

agentSessionId.description: The coding-agent session the call belongs to.

chatSessionId.description: The chat session the call belongs to (metadata only, never its content).

inputTokens.description: Prompt tokens, as the ledger charged them; null for a released call, whose tokens nobody reported.

outputTokens.description: Completion tokens, as the ledger charged them; null for a released call.

reservedUsd.description: What Nexus Gateway held for the call before it ran.

reason.description: The ledger's note on the call, with any secret redacted: why it was refused, failed or released, or what it charged past its hold.

overspendLevel.description: The spend limit that refused the call.

overspendLimitUsd.description: The person's limit, when a person's limit refused the call. Null for a team's cap and the organization's budget: the ledger does not keep their limit on the call.

overspendAmountUsd.description: What the refused call asked to hold.

overspendOverUsd.description: How far over the limit it would have gone.

fundedBy.description: `nexus_subsidy` for a call a Nexus subsidy paid, `nexus_credit` for one the organization's prepaid credits paid; null for the organization's own.

SpendCallPage.description: One page of spend calls, newest first.

from.description: The first UTC day the page covers.

to.description: The last UTC day the page covers, included.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next, older page; null on the last page.

UsageRow.description: The calls of one UTC day, team, person, model, provider and product, summed. Every Analytics view is a sum of these rows. Settled, failed and released calls count, as in Analytics; refused calls are left out. Every field is always present, and an unknown value is null. People and teams are named by id only; their names are in the directory file (`exportDirectoryCsv`). Money is a decimal string in US dollars with six decimals. A CSV file has one column per field, in this order.

teamId.description: The team; null for calls with no team (`unassigned`).

userId.description: The person; null for calls with no person.

model.description: The model; null for released calls, whose model the ledger did not record.

provider.description: The provider; null for released calls.

AgentSessionRow.description: One coding-agent session. Its folder, its email and the agent's own conversation id are left out. Every field is always present, and an unknown value is null. People and teams are named by id only; their names are in the directory file (`exportDirectoryCsv`). Money is a decimal string in US dollars with six decimals. A CSV file has one column per field, in this order.

model.description: The model the session started on.

via.description: `nexus`: its model calls went through Nexus Gateway; `subscription`: the person's own plan; `ori`: sessions from before Nexus Gateway carried agents' calls.

access.description: Who pays its model calls, as Nexus Gateway classified the session when it opened.

teamId.description: The team it was attributed to.

calls.description: Its model calls through Nexus Gateway, refused calls left out.

reportedCalls.description: `subscription` sessions: the calls the agent reported.

reportedInputTokens.description: `subscription` sessions: the input tokens the agent reported.

reportedOutputTokens.description: `subscription` sessions: the output tokens the agent reported.

reportedCacheReadTokens.description: `subscription` sessions: the cache reads the agent reported.

reportedCacheCreationTokens.description: `subscription` sessions: the cache writes the agent reported.

estimatedCostUsd.description: `subscription` sessions: the agent's list-price estimate. Never charged: the person's plan pays.

DirectoryEntry.description: One person or team of the organization, with its name: the one file that maps ids to names. Every field is always present, and an unknown value is null.

id.description: The user id or the team id the data files name.

name.description: The person's or the team's name, read when the file is made. Null for an erased person, a person with no record and a deleted team.

slug.description: A team's slug; null for a person and for a deleted team.

parentId.description: The team a team sits under; null for a top-level team, a deleted team and a person.

erased.description: A person whose personal data was erased: `name` is null.

ExportManifest.description: What one exported file holds, so a reader can tell a complete file from a cut or damaged one. A JSON Lines file ends with one line `{"manifest": …}`. A CSV file carries none: its manifest is `metadata.manifest` on its audit event (`GET /v1/audit?target=<exportId>`). It proves completeness, not authenticity or freshness.

exportId.description: The export's id: the `x-nexus-export-id` header, and its audit event's target id.

schemaVersion.description: The row's version. A changed column raises it.

scope.description: Who asked, and the filters as Nexus Gateway applied them, defaults included.

range.description: The UTC days the file covers; null for the directory file.

rows.description: The file's rows, without the CSV header or the manifest line.

checksum.description: SHA-256 of every byte of a CSV file, or of every JSON Lines line before the manifest line.

watermark.description: Opaque: the point in the records the file was cut at. Records written after it are not in the file. Null for the directory file.

complete.description: False when the row limit (100,000 rows a file) cut the file: `nextCursor` gives the rest. Also false, with `nextCursor` null, in the audit event of a stream that failed or that the client left (`metadata.cut: true`).

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` with the same query for the next file; null when the file is complete.

policyVersion.description: The version of the policy that allowed the read; null until policies are versioned.

integrity.description: No proof of integrity travels with the file: Nexus Gateway proves integrity for the audit log only.

oneOf.description: One event the item reports, as ids: a refused call's spend record, an access request or report on an artifact, a billing change's audit row, a billing month whose payment failed, a person who joined, a skill promotion, a security change's audit action, the provider of a rejected key, the answer to the person's own access request, a GitHub App installation that lost repositories, a closed month's usage report, a spend limit change's audit action, a referral by a hash of the referred person's id, a state of the organization's money, or a member's question to the owners about a billing block, or a Policy approval record that waits on the person, or a cloud session whose state moved.

auditId.description: The billing change's audit row, for `billing_change`

action.description: The audit action of a security change, such as key.revoked, or of a limit change, such as budget.team_changed

provider.description: The provider of a rejected key, for `provider_key`

outcome.description: How the author answered the person's access request, for `artifact_access_answer`

installationId.description: The Nexus GitHub App installation's GitHub id, for `github_installation`

month.description: The closed UTC calendar month, `YYYY-MM`, for `usage_month`

referral.description: A hash of the referred person's id, never the id, for `referral`

block.description: What stops the member who asked, for `owner_ask` (`userId` is that member)

approvalId.description: The Policy approval record (`apr_…`) that waits on the person, for `approval`

machineId.description: The cloud machine the session runs on, for `session`

threadId.description: The session's workbench thread on the machine, for `session`

seq.description: The session's event that moved its state, for `session`

NotificationItem.description: One item in your inbox. It holds ids only: show `subjectText` and link each source to its own page, which checks its own permission.

kind.description: The kind's stable name, as GET /v1/notifications/kinds lists it

title.description: A month report's summary, from its figures only: the month and the total. Absent for other kinds

detail.description: A month report's second line, from its figures only: the calls. Absent for other kinds

count.description: The events this item collapses; it can pass the 20 sources kept

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last

required.description: A required kind can move between channels but never be muted

name.description: The provider (`anthropic`, or `anthropic:team:team_…` for a team's key), or the connector and its scope (`linear:user:usr_…`).

sealedWith.description: `data_key`: the organization's data key of version `keyVersion`. `nexus_secret`: a key derived from a server setting, sealed before data keys. `reference`: no secret is held, only a reference to a vendor's short-lived token.

holder.description: `nexus_secret`: derived from Nexus's a server setting. `nexus_kms`: a Cloud KMS key in Nexus's project. `customer_kms`: a Cloud KMS key in the customer's own project; the customer can revoke Nexus's access.

key.description: The customer's Cloud KMS key's resource name; absent when Nexus holds the master.

plan.description: Written by Billing: an entry of Billing Capabilities' plan catalogue; null until one is chosen.

payerUserId.description: The member who pays; null until named.

billingContactUserId.description: The member who receives billing mail; null until named.

periodStart.description: Written by Billing: the first day of the paid term.

periodEnd.description: Written by Billing: the day the paid term ends; null for an open term.

status.description: Written by Billing alone. It changes what the organization is entitled to, never who is in it.

effectiveAt.description: When the newest change took effect.

updatedAt.description: When the subscription was last written; null until its first change.

seats.description: One per member that `GET /v1/orgs/members` lists, counted when read.

changed.description: The fields that changed, or would change on a dry run; empty when nothing did.

OperatorGrant.description: An operator's access to a customer's organization, for a reason, a list of actions and a time. It makes no member and no seat.

tenantId.description: The customer organization the grant reaches.

operator.description: The operator who holds the grant. The name and the email are read from their user record when the grant is read; nothing stores them with the grant or in the customer's audit log.

scope.description: The actions the operator may do, by name in the permission matrix.

revokedBy.description: The person who revoked it: the operator, or an owner or admin of the customer.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor, while more items follow. Only when limit or cursor was sent.

scope.description: The actions the operator may do, by name in the permission matrix. Each is one an admin may do and none that spends money, acts as a person, or changes access, credentials, limits or settings.

expiresAt.description: In the future, at most 7 days from now. 24 hours from now by default.

dryRun.description: A dry run's id is never used.

removedBy.description: The user id who removed them; absent when the sign-in provider did.

teams.description: The slugs of the teams they come back to.

deleted.description: False on a dry run; true once the account is deleted.

personalOrg.description: Your personal organization's id, closed with the account; absent when you have none.

planEnded.description: Whether your personal organization's plan and cards at the payment provider end with it.

signInNeeded.description: Whether you must sign in again first: only a sign-in from the last ten minutes deletes your account.

unpaidUsageUsd.description: Your personal organization's usage that its card has not paid, as a decimal dollar string. On a dry run, what the deletion charges to the card on file first. Once deleted, what that charge did not collect, which Nexus writes off. Absent when nothing is unpaid.

creditsLostUsd.description: Your personal organization's Nexus credits that the deletion loses, as a decimal dollar string. Nothing refunds them. Absent when none are left.

at.description: When the organization first reached it; null when it has not, or when `error` says it could not be read

minutesAfterSignup.description: Whole minutes from `signedUpAt` to `at`; 0 for a value recorded before the sign-up

exact.description: False when older records were pruned or not listed, so the true first may be earlier than `at`

error.description: `wiki_not_configured` or `wiki_unavailable`: why the value could not be read; the rest of the answer stands

mark.description: The organization's mark; null for a customer's. A figure that leaves the organization counts a marked one apart

tenantZero.description: Whether the organization is marked staff: Nexus's own, where C1 is measured. A figure that leaves it counts it apart

signedUpAt.description: The organization's creation: every `minutesAfterSignup` counts from it

activated.description: Activated by either definition: the earlier of `gateway` and `wiki`. Exact only when both are; carries the Wiki's `error`, since an unknown Wiki run may be the earlier

gateway.description: Activated: Gateway. The first agent session through nexus claude or nexus codex

wiki.description: Activated: Wiki. The first Nexus Wiki run

firstSettledCall.description: The first model call that settled; refused and failed calls do not count

teams.description: Team slugs (a deleted team's id); null for the whole organization

default.description: The connector's default: the organization never chose

offered.description: Whether this Gateway offers the connector. The organization's choice of one it does not offer is kept; no one uses it, and it may only be set to disabled

teams.description: Team slugs; leave it out for the whole organization

mark.description: The organization's mark, as in GrowthActivation

tenantZero.description: Whether the organization is marked staff, as in GrowthActivation

members.description: The organization's members now with no mark; a removed member is not counted

markedMembers.description: Its members marked staff, test or demo; no step counts them. At an organization marked staff, staff stay in members

steps.description: Every step, over the members with no mark, in order

stall.description: The step the most members stopped just before (the earlier one on a tie); null when no one stopped short

waiting.description: Members whose furthest step is the one before it: they stopped there

waitMinutes.description: Whole minutes from each member's previous step reached to this one, never below 0; null for joined, and below five waits, so no one person's wait shows

exact.description: False when older records were pruned or not read, so a member may have reached it earlier, or at all

WaitMinutes.description: A distribution of waits in whole minutes, by nearest rank

kind.description: `error`: an error in the app's JavaScript; `crash`: a native crash (the OS's, or a desktop panic) seen at the next start

name.description: The error's name (`TypeError`), or the crash's exception and signal

message.description: The error's message, already redacted by the app; may be empty

stack.description: The top frames: a function and its place in the bundle, or a binary and its offset

appBuild.description: The store build number, when the app knows it

osVersion.description: The OS version the report came from

accepted.description: How many reports went to the log

category.description: What it is. `crash` carries `crash`, and only it does; `report` carries `answer`, and only it does; `triage` is a report that `nexus triage`'s agent wrote, sent only by Nexus's own people to the triage channel

message.description: What the person wrote: 1 to 4000 characters (12000 with `triage`), or empty with a crash or a report. Slack shows it as plain text

screen.description: The screen the person was on, as its route's shape (`/acme/sessions/:id`): letters, digits and / _ . ~ - :, never a query

appBuild.description: The build, when the app knows it

osVersion.description: The OS's version, or the browser's

crash.description: The crash the app saw at this start, which the person chose to send; logged as a diagnostic report too

answer.description: With the category `report`: the model's answer the person reported, as the app showed it

ReportedAnswer.description: A model's answer that a person reported (App Review 1.2), and why. Slack shows the text as plain text

reason.description: Why: `offensive` (offensive, abusive or harmful), `wrong` (wrong or misleading) or `other`

text.description: The answer's text as the app showed it, not only white space. The app cuts a longer answer to 12000 characters

model.description: The model that wrote it, when the app knows it: one line, no control character

code.description: Your referral code: ten random characters of lowercase base 32, made on the first read. A code made earlier from your name gets one on its next read, and the old code still works.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor, while more people follow.

invitesLeft.description: While sign-up is invite-only: how many more people your code admits, as an operator approved. Only the people who joined through your code after the approval use one. Absent while sign-up is open, and for a staff member's code with no approval, which admits anyone.

invitesAllowed.description: While sign-up is invite-only: how many people an operator approved your code to admit in all, used or not. `0`: not approved. With `invitesLeft` `0` and this above `0`, you used every invitation. Absent while sign-up is open, for a staff member's code with no approval, and on older Gateways.

enabled.description: False while the personal referral program is stopped. Existing referrals remain readable.

rewardsGranted.description: How many referral rewards your personal organization got in all, across all pages, including credit already spent or expired, limit or not. Absent on older Gateways.

rewardUsdDecimal.description: What one rewarded referral gives your personal organization, in US dollars with six decimals (`"1.000000"`). `"0.000000"` while no reward is set. Absent on older Gateways.

rewardsActive.description: Whether your referrals earn rewards now: the program is on, a reward and a program cap are set, the cap has room for one more reward, and you are below your lifetime limit (`rewardProgress`) or are staff, who have none. False: no referral of yours earns credit now. Absent on older Gateways, which a client reads as false.

email.description: Their email with all but its first character before the `@` hidden (`a***@example.com`). `null` when they erased their account (`erased`), or when their sign-in carried no email Nexus could keep.

erased.description: Whether the person erased their account. A person with no email who is not erased is still live: a reward needs their email. Absent on older Gateways, which a client reads from a `null` email.

rewarded.description: Whether this referral earned the caller a reward. Absent or null when unavailable. No payment date is disclosed.

reward.description: This referral's reward. `pending`: none yet, and one may come; a payment is never disclosed while a reward can still come. `rewarded`: your personal organization got it. `not_rewarded`: final, it never will (its reward was voided, you reached the lifetime limit, or you have no personal organization). Absent on older Gateways.

AccountMark.description: Why an organization or a person is Nexus's own: `staff`, `test` or `demo`

mark.description: The mark now; null for a customer's account
The mark, or null to clear it

BillingPlan.description: A plan's subscription as Stripe keeps it

plan.description: A plan in a server setting, such as plus, pro, teams_plus or teams_pro

AfterTheFact.description: Paying after the fact (pricing v2.0): the card on file pays for what Nexus runs after it ran, at provider price plus Nexus's rate, up to a monthly usage limit. Gateway's Stripe sweep charges the card each time the unpaid usage reaches `thresholdUsd`; less carries over, and what is left is charged once it is turned off. A charge that fails stops the calls the card pays (402 `payment_failed`) until one goes through. While a charge runs (`pending`, such as a bank debit Stripe is still taking), the card holds a new call only while the unpaid usage, the charge's own amount included, and the calls it holds stay within twice `thresholdUsd`; past that the call answers 402 `charge_processing` until the charge is paid, and `nexusPays.reason` says `charge_processing`. Decimal dollar strings.

phase.description: Where the card's charge lifecycle is. Read it instead of deriving a state from the other fields. The first that holds wins: `closed` (the organization closed; the row never charges again), `disputed` (a payment on the card was disputed; it ends with another card or a won dispute), `needs_confirmation` (the bank wants the cardholder to confirm the charge, 3-D Secure), `retrying` (a charge failed and a new try runs now) or `failed` (the next try waits), `charging` (a charge runs: Stripe's answer, or a bank debit Stripe is still taking), `on`, then `off_owing` (off, with usage still unpaid) or `off`. Calls on the card stop in `failed`, `retrying`, `needs_confirmation` and `disputed` (402 `payment_failed`).

unpaidUsd.description: The usage the card has not paid: spent less paid, a running charge included. Name this amount when a charge failed or runs: `owedUsd` leaves a running charge out, so it is about zero during a retry.

A call may be refused while `leftUsd` is above zero: its most possible cost is more than what is left. Null when no call was refused this month.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters (a UUID). The first request runs and its answer is kept 24 hours; a repeat with the same method, path and body gets it again with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different request is 422 `idempotency_key_reused`; a repeat while the first runs is 409 `idempotency_in_progress`; a repeat after the first was cut off before it answered (504 `timeout`, or the connection closed) is 409 `idempotency_interrupted`, as it may have run in part; a finished streamed model call is never replayed (409 `idempotency_stream_replay`) or charged twice; a stream whose call failed (cut, provider error) gives its key back, so a retry runs. Answers of 500+ and 429 are not kept.

BadRequest.description: The request is not valid; the message names the field. A JSON body that is not an object, or a string in it that holds U+0000 (`nul_in_string`), is a 400 on every route that reads one. So is an `Idempotency-Key` that is not 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters (`invalid_idempotency_key`).

Unauthorized.description: No credential (`missing_credential`), or a credential Gateway does not accept (`invalid_credential`).

Forbidden.description: The caller may not do this: for example, the role does not have the permission (`role_required`), or the team named is not the caller's (`not_in_team`).

NotFound.description: Nothing matches. A path parameter outside its pattern is a 404 "no such endpoint", before the credential is checked. A team named that does not exist is `unknown_team`.

RequestTimeout.description: The request body stopped arriving for 30 seconds, or took longer than 10 minutes in all (`request_timeout`; `nexus` holds `gap_seconds` and `total_seconds`).

IdempotencyConflict.description: The `Idempotency-Key` cannot run or replay: its first request still runs (`idempotency_in_progress`), was a stream (`idempotency_stream_replay`), or its answer was not kept, being over 2,000,000 bytes (`idempotency_response_not_stored`). The request does not run again.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body is over the operation's limit (`request_too_large`): 1,000,000 bytes, unless the operation says otherwise.

IdempotencyKeyReused.description: The `Idempotency-Key` was used for a different request: another method, path, query or body (`idempotency_key_reused`).

UpgradeRequired.description: The `nexus` CLI that sent `x-nexus-cli-version` is older than Gateway supports (`cli_too_old`; `minimum` names the oldest it takes). A request without that header is never refused.

Unavailable.description: Gateway takes no new request now: it is at its limit of requests in flight (`overloaded`), or it is stopping (`draining`). Retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait: 1 when Gateway is at its limit, 5 when it is stopping.

GatewayTimeout.description: The request passed Gateway's deadline, 30 seconds by default (`timeout`). Model calls that may stream are outside it.

ProviderBadRequest.description: The request is not valid: for example, it has no `model`, or its body is not UTF-8, not a JSON object, or repeats a field. So is an `Idempotency-Key` that is not 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters (`invalid_idempotency_key`).

ProviderUnauthorized.description: No key (`missing_credential`; send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key`), or a key Gateway does not accept (`invalid_credential`).

ProviderForbidden.description: The caller may not do this: for example, the role does not have the permission (`role_required`), or the team named is not the caller's (`not_in_team`).

ProviderNotFound.description: The team named in `x-nexus-team` does not exist (`unknown_team`).

ProviderRequestTimeout.description: The request body stopped arriving for 30 seconds, or took longer than 10 minutes in all (`request_timeout`; `nexus` holds `gap_seconds` and `total_seconds`).

ProviderIdempotencyConflict.description: The `Idempotency-Key` cannot run or replay: its first request still runs (`idempotency_in_progress`), was a stream (`idempotency_stream_replay`), or its answer was not kept, being over 2,000,000 bytes (`idempotency_response_not_stored`). The request does not run again.

ProviderPayloadTooLarge.description: The request body is over 32,000,000 bytes, the agent gateway's limit (`request_too_large`).

ProviderIdempotencyKeyReused.description: The `Idempotency-Key` was used for a different request: another method, path, query or body (`idempotency_key_reused`).

ProviderUpgradeRequired.description: The `nexus` CLI that sent `x-nexus-cli-version` is older than Gateway supports (`cli_too_old`; `minimum` names the oldest it takes). A request without that header is never refused.

ProviderUpstreamFailed.description: The provider could not be reached, or the connection to it failed (`api_error`).

ProviderCallUnavailable.description: The provider's or the Gateway's own; every one may be retried. The provider's: its own 503 passes through as it wrote it, with its `retry-after` (OpenAI's overload; Anthropic's is a 529, not a 503); `/metrics` and the request log count it as `upstream_overloaded`. Retry after its wait, or try another model. The Gateway's, in the provider's error shape: it is at its limit of requests in flight (`overloaded`, retry after 1 s); it is stopping and takes no new request (`draining`, retry after 5 s); it stopped before the call answered (`gateway_stopping`, send the call again: it reaches a running Gateway); or its database is busy (`database_busy`: nothing was committed, retry shortly).

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait: 1 on `overloaded`, 5 on `draining`, the provider's own on its 503 when it sent one; none on `gateway_stopping` or `database_busy`.

ProviderCountUnavailable.description: The provider's or the Gateway's own; every one may be retried. The provider's: its own 503 passes through as it wrote it, with its `retry-after` (OpenAI's overload; Anthropic's is a 529, not a 503); `/metrics` and the request log count it as `upstream_overloaded`. Retry after its wait, or try another model. The Gateway's, in the provider's error shape: it is at its limit of requests in flight (`overloaded`, retry after 1 s); it is stopping and takes no new request (`draining`, retry after 5 s); or its database is busy (`database_busy`, retry shortly). A count is never `gateway_stopping`.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait: 1 on `overloaded`, 5 on `draining`, the provider's own on its 503 when it sent one; none on `database_busy`.

ProviderUnavailable.description: Gateway takes no new request now: it is at its limit of requests in flight (`overloaded`), or it is stopping (`draining`). Retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait: 1 when Gateway is at its limit, 5 when it is stopping.

ProviderUpstreamTimeout.description: The provider passed one of the call's deadlines (`upstream_timeout`; `nexus.phase` names which).

RateLimit-Limit.description: The most requests the caller may make in one window (a fixed minute, per caller).

RateLimit-Remaining.description: The requests the caller has left in this window.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Whole seconds until the window starts over.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before trying again: the same as `RateLimit-Reset`.

x-nexus-export-id.description: The export's id (`exp_…`): the target id of its audit event, which holds a CSV file's manifest.
